## The dispositional reframing, withdrawn before merge

A52 §17's synthesis, with A55 §11 and A58 §10 as later versions, was
filed in this pull request as a Proposed CLAIM, at version 3, under a
temporary code. It did not pass [ADR-075](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-075.md)'s admission test by any of
its three routes, so the owner directed that it be withdrawn before
merge, not retired by status. Its content is not refuted: every clause is
held by the entries the admission section names. No permanent code was
ever assigned. What it said, and its audit, are kept here.

**Title as filed.** The organized possibility in which the record's account locates an individual is dispositional: what a declared bearer would manifest across declared conditions, grounded in its actual organization and persisting while unmanifested; so disposition is a dimension of the capacities, perspectives, concepts and will-organizations the record already names, not a further layer or object, and an individual's dispositional profile is its character, not its identity; and its dispositional equivalence to another, its historical continuity, its numerical identity and its autonomy are four properties, none following from another

**Summary as filed.** The thesis of U22 to U24 of the exchange "Individuation, Possibility, and Disposition" (2026-11-06 to 07), from A47 §9 to A52 §17, the version filed and the exchange's last account. The reframing is the owner's: U22 asked whether "disposition" might be "a clarifying tool (not necessarily a new thing, could be an improved reframing of a term of art we've already adopted)", and the term filed from it is [TERM-118](../../record/terms.d/TERM-118.md). A52 tells it as "The recent turn to dispositions" and uses the owner's [TERM-086](../../record/terms.d/TERM-086.md) phrase "organizational achievement" without citing it. The integration is A's, from A47 §8 and §9. A52 §2 makes dispositional organization a layer of its own, against A47 and A50; the claim takes A47's form. The audit finds it the thinnest of the exchange's syntheses, mostly a renaming of held distinctions. Version 2 takes A55 §11's four-way independence clause and success test, from the second share; A55 tells the owner's U4, U6, U14 to U16, U18 and U22 as what the work "taught us", and they are credited here. It reframes the thesis on meaning and will ([CLAIM-620](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-620.md)) and rests on the two on possibility and history. The integration's wording is A's, corrected by the filer; adopting it is the owner's call.

**defeated_if as filed.** Some part of the account that is not dispositional: a capacity, perspective or will-organization the record attributes to a bearer that makes no difference to what it would manifest under any declared condition, or a merely possible manifestation, with no ground in the bearer's actual organization, that individuation must still count. Or two individuals the record must count as one although they differ in dispositional profile and in nothing else, so that the profile is identity after all. Also defeated as a thesis of its own if it only restates [TERM-118](../../record/terms.d/TERM-118.md) with [CLAIM-421](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-421.md) (dispositions outlast enactment), [CLAIM-287](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-287.md) (persistence as capacity to reinstate) and [TERM-086](../../record/terms.d/TERM-086.md)'s dispositional mode, with "disposition" put where those say capacity. A52 §16 concedes the risk: "The novel contribution cannot be simply renaming those phenomena." Not defeated by an observed behaviour that misleads about the disposition (masking, mimicking, finks), which the claim expects. Also defeated if the dispositional account tells apart no pair of organizations matched under ordinary observation that [CLAIM-414](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-414.md), [CLAIM-407](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-407.md), [CLAIM-521](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-521.md) and [CLAIM-522](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md) do not already tell apart. A55 §11 states that test: "whether the enriched theory can distinguish organizations that look the same under ordinary observation but differ in what they are capable of doing, what determines whether those capacities become effective, how those capacities are maintained, and what survives when the organization changes". And defeated in its last clause by a case in which one of the four properties follows from another, as identity would from an identical profile.

#### The claim

A52 §17: "These relationships ground a structured repertoire of
dispositions: possible manifestations across relevant circumstances,
including capacities not currently exercised." "The individual is not
simply its present state, its current collective mode, or its
dispositional profile." A47 §9: "**My strongest recommendation is to treat
disposition as the modal dimension of organizational capacity, not as a new
ontological primitive or a replacement for will.**" A50 §11: "**organized
possibility that has a real causal basis, even when it is not presently
manifest.**"

The architecture, in layers:

1. **What is dispositional.** The repertoire [CLAIM-611](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-611.md) (Proposed, A's)
   says persists. In [TERM-118](../../record/terms.d/TERM-118.md)'s terms (Proposed, the owner's U22, A's
   wording) it is an ability across declared conditions, or a tendency to
   manifest. Vetter's split between "fragile" and "breakable" is the
   record's source for the two ([THEORY-670](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-670.md), Proposed; [LIT-109](../../record/literature.d/LIT-109.md) and [NOTE-125](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-125.md),
   Read).

   The repertoire has three dimensions (A58 §10, second share, answering
   the owner's U26): the **discriminative**, "What circumstances can the
   organization distinguish?", which is [TERM-064](../../record/terms.d/TERM-064.md)'s legibility; the
   **practical**, "What actions can it undertake in those circumstances?";
   and the **transformative**, "How can it revise its distinctions,
   actions, and the relationships governing them?", which is [TERM-023](../../record/terms.d/TERM-023.md)'s
   transformation, with [CLAIM-025](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-025.md) and [CLAIM-532](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-532.md). "The first two jointly
   determine which tasks it can perform", as [CLAIM-535](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-535.md) and [CLAIM-572](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-572.md) do:
   a hedge can stand in for a distinction. *The reader's correction:* A
   drops [CASE-194](../../record/cases.d/CASE-194.md)'s third repair, authority, which lies between the
   practical and the transformative.
2. **It persists while unmanifested.** A47 §9: "a disposition provides a way
   of describing continuity through nonmanifestation". The record holds it.
   A perspective's enactment can stop while its dispositions remain
   ([CLAIM-421](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-421.md), Active). What persists through inactivity is the capacity to
   reinstate ([CLAIM-287](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-287.md), Active). Possessing a regime is not its being
   effective ([CLAIM-047](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-047.md), Active).
3. **A dimension of the existing terms.** The motivating perspective is
   "motivating as a disposition" ([TERM-104](../../record/terms.d/TERM-104.md), Proposed, the owner's U28 of
   2026-11-04). The dispositional mode of an organizational achievement is
   [TERM-086](../../record/terms.d/TERM-086.md)'s (Proposed, the owner's term). A disposition is read through a
   governance-response profile ([TERM-067](../../record/terms.d/TERM-067.md), Active).
4. **Character, not identity.** A52 §11 and A47 §7: an identical profile in
   a fork does not give one individual. Identity over time stays with
   [CLAIM-615](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-615.md) (Proposed).

What the integration adds is A52's "And now we can see how these are
connected through dispositions": the claim that one modal notion, borne by
a declared bearer, is the common dimension of the record's capacity,
perspective, concept and will terms.

#### Corrections to A's version

- **Correction (fidelity): a dimension, not a layer.** A52 §2 lists
  "**Dispositional organization**" among "five fundamental layers". A52
  calls them aspects, "not necessarily separate physical components". Even
  so, this goes against A47 §9 ("not as a new ontological primitive") and
  against A50 §11: "This seems preferable to introducing *disposition* as
  one more object alongside all the others." The title takes A47's form.
- **Correction (fidelity): the declared bearer.** [TERM-019](../../record/terms.d/TERM-019.md) (Active) retired
  "disposition" because it "had been carrying both the person-level and the
  institution-level reading". A47 §8 respected that, and A50 and A52 do
  not mention it. A50 §6 then gives a community a "disposition to reject
  unilateral governance changes". The title says "a declared bearer", as
  [TERM-118](../../record/terms.d/TERM-118.md) does.
- **Correction (fidelity): ability and tendency.** A47 §2 separates them
  ("A person may know how to perform a task and be disposed to avoid
  performing it"). A47 §9's "modal dimension of organizational capacity"
  folds the tendency sense back into capacity. Layer 1 keeps both.
- **Correction (fidelity): Vetter.** A50 §2: "She challenges the assumption
  that each disposition must be defined by one specified stimulus followed
  by one specified response". It then models dispositions as
  stimulus-conditioned kernels, the conditional conception Vetter argues
  against ([NOTE-125](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-125.md)). A's profile is [TERM-067](../../record/terms.d/TERM-067.md)'s kind of characterization,
  and Vetter is its rival, not its support.
- **Correction (fidelity): numerical identity.** A52 §16 says [CLAIM-150](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-150.md)
  "already establishes this caution" that indistinguishable organizations
  need not be numerically identical. [CLAIM-150](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-150.md) is about constitution.
  Numerical identity is [CLAIM-329](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-329.md) and [CLAIM-287](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-287.md).
- **Correction (attribution and coverage).** A52 §1's "The recent turn to
  dispositions" is the owner's U22, and the owner guessed right that the
  word reframes an adopted term. A52 drops A47's [TERM-019](../../record/terms.d/TERM-019.md) warning, A50's
  mimicking case, the fork as a new channel for a suppressed disposition
  ([CLAIM-613](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-613.md), Proposed), Swidler and habitus ([LIT-1367](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1367.md), [LIT-1377](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1377.md);
  [ARG-025](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-025.md)'s competitor), and A50 §3's caution that an intervention can
  change the disposition it probes.
- **Correction (standing).** A52 §1: "we have reached a more precise and
  more ambitious formulation". The terms it rests on are Proposed
  ([TERM-118](../../record/terms.d/TERM-118.md), [TERM-086](../../record/terms.d/TERM-086.md), [TERM-104](../../record/terms.d/TERM-104.md), [THEORY-670](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-670.md)).

- **Correction (attribution), version 2.** A55 §11 tells the inquiry's
  course as what the work "taught us", crediting no turn. "The synergetic
  and coordination-dynamics work" is the owner's U4 laboratory
  ("synchronization phenomena might be a useful laboratory") and U6's
  timescale question. "The software-project examples taught us" is the
  owner's U14 (software product), U15 (PyTorch, and "a form of
  Structuralism") and U16 (the contested succession, [CASE-223](../../record/cases.d/CASE-223.md)). "The
  meaning inquiry" is joined at the owner's U18 ("connect this to
  Nuckeation's inquiry examining how meaning works"). "the dispositional
  turn" is the owner's U22, uncredited again, as in A52 §1. Its first
  clause, that productive organization "can survive implementation
  replacement", is [CLAIM-280](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-280.md) (Active), held before the exchange.
- **Correction (standing), version 2.** The four-way clause is held
  piecewise: isomorphism is not persistence ([CLAIM-593](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-593.md), Active), persistence
  is by transmission ([CLAIM-329](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-329.md), Proposed), and autonomy is a sense of its
  own ([TERM-088](../../record/terms.d/TERM-088.md)). It generalizes layer 4, "character, not identity", and
  is a guard rather than a new integration.

#### What it does not say

- **That dispositions are a new ontological primitive**, per A47 §9.
- **That a concept bears dispositions.** A47 §8: "an abstract concept need
  not itself be a causal bearer of dispositions. The dispositions are
  realized in its interpreters and the organizations sustaining its use".
- **That a profile measured on conflicts actually won reads the
  disposition.** That is [QUESTION-268](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-268.md) (Open).

#### Versions

A47's opening, "**An organization is characterized not only by what it is
doing, or by the structures it presently realizes, but by what it is
disposed to do, recognize, sustain, resist, or transform under different
circumstances.**", and §9: "**An individual is a historically continuous
organization of realized relationships and maintained dispositions through
which a distinguishable repertoire of possible activities and
transformations is sustained.**" A50 §11: "**An individual is a historically
continuous organization whose causal relationships realize, regulate, and
transform a structured repertoire of dispositions.**" A52 §1 and §17 are
the version filed for version 1. Its clauses on meaning and will restate [CLAIM-620](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-620.md),
which this claim reframes and does not replace.

A55 §11 (second share,
https://chatgpt.com/share/6aeea2bc-d280-83e9-ac1f-f6772adf263c), the
"candidate synthesis statement", is the source of version 2: "**Organizational
individuation may be understood through the historical production,
regulation, and transmission of structured dispositions.**" "These
capabilities can remain latent, become effective, be suppressed, lose
their productive basis, or be transformed into new capacities." "Concepts
and perspectives can be reproduced across changing bearers, while their
historical continuities may diverge from the continuity of symbols,
institutions, or individual agents." "**Dispositional equivalence,
historical continuity, numerical identity, and organizational autonomy
remain distinct properties.** None follows automatically from the others."
A: "It prevents the dispositional vocabulary from becoming another
universal identity criterion that silently resolves questions we've
explicitly left open." Its integrating sentence is A50 §11's, and its
clauses on meaning and will restate [CLAIM-620](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-620.md) and on transmission
[CLAIM-615](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-615.md).

#### Admission

Under [ADR-075](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-075.md)'s admission test, a synthesis is filed only if its integration can fail while every component holds. This one cannot. "Persists while unmanifested" is [CLAIM-421](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-421.md), [CLAIM-287](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-287.md) and [CLAIM-047](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-047.md); "character, not identity" is [CLAIM-593](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-593.md) with [CLAIM-615](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-615.md); the four-way independence is held piecewise by [CLAIM-593](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-593.md), [CLAIM-329](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-329.md) and [TERM-088](../../record/terms.d/TERM-088.md); and "a dimension, not a layer" is the vocabulary [TERM-118](../../record/terms.d/TERM-118.md) already chose. The one candidate is the grounding clause. Left free ("a declared bearer"), it absorbs any externally grounded possibility by declaring a wider bearer, so no case can be stated. Fixed as the individual, it is defeated by [CLAIM-522](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)'s outside controller, which keeps a repertoire realizable that is not grounded in the individual's own organization, and that construction is a premise of this claim through [CLAIM-611](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-611.md). Its success test names no pair the dispositional account separates and [CLAIM-414](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-414.md), [CLAIM-407](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-407.md), [CLAIM-521](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-521.md) and [CLAIM-522](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md) do not. Retired by status, Rejected; the record keeps it and its audit.

The first synthesis review, run as [ADR-078](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-078.md)'s demonstration under the
`synthesis-review` skill. Four read-only readers audited the shortlist,
three candidates each, with [ADR-075](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-075.md)'s five checks and three admission
routes. Each checked its quotes of six words or more mechanically (every one
matching) and reran the mathematics. The filer checked the
admitted drafts against the entries before filing. The readers could not
write their reports to files in this harness. Their reports were saved
from their messages to the session's scratchpad; this entry keeps what
they found.

## The ranking

`scratch/formal/synthesis_candidates.py` found 627 claims, 569 in force,
and 5 syntheses. It ranked:

- **Arm A:** 33 CLAIMs with three or more premises across two or more
  lines. The top six were [CLAIM-545](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-545.md) (21), [CLAIM-556](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-556.md) (19), [CLAIM-534](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-534.md) (18),
  [CLAIM-191](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-191.md) (17), [CLAIM-532](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-532.md) (16) and [CLAIM-474](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-474.md) (16).
- **Arm B1:** 24 `complements` clusters within one line. The largest were
  realizability (12 claims), pragmatic-transport (7), nucleating-argument
  (7), formal-apparatus (6) and evidence-for-experience (5).
- **Arm B2:** 16 open questions with three or more unintegrated answers,
  led by [QUESTION-398](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-398.md), [QUESTION-380](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-380.md) and [QUESTION-131](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-131.md).
- **Arm B3:** 51 Active theses at `rests_on` depth three or more, led by
  [CLAIM-560](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-560.md), [CLAIM-556](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-556.md) and [CLAIM-554](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-554.md) at depth 6.

**Added by hand**, in [CLAIM-545](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-545.md)'s audit:

- A26 of the exchange "Organizational Nucleation and SLT", which the
  workbench calls a consolidated thesis;
- A's synthesis THEORY from the curation entry of 2026-11-05 (214041).

[QUESTION-398](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-398.md) and [QUESTION-399](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-399.md) were audited with the realizability cluster

## [CLAIM-474](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-474.md): admitted, its move left to the owner

[CLAIM-474](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-474.md) passes the hypothesis route. The case is a stipulated theorem
that persistence of a robust boundary implies partial self-production. Its
"special classes" exemption needs a bound.

Moving it into the scheme would demote it. It is Active by a status-review
ruling the owner delegated, but a review files every SYNTHESIS as Proposed
and never sets one Current. It would also lose relations, because SYNTHESIS
has no `grounds`, `uses` or `corroborated_by`.

So it stays an Active CLAIM. Two things are for the owner:

- whether to move it and set the synthesis Current at once;
- whether the scheme should gain those fields first.

If it moves, these would be repointed:

- [CASE-179](../../record/cases.d/CASE-179.md)'s `illustrates`;
- [SYNTHESIS-004](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-004.md)'s `integrates` and `premises`.

## Found along the way

- **Split temporary codes.** Four temporary codes in [SYNTHESIS-002](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-002.md),
  [SYNTHESIS-005](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-005.md), [CLAIM-620](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-620.md) and [CLAIM-624](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-624.md) had been split across a line
  break, so merge-time numbering missed them. They are repaired in their
  own pull request (dmarx/nucleation#426). Whoever wraps prose by hand
  should keep a code on one line.
- **For a later review:**
  - **[CLAIM-600](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md)**, which the notes on [QUESTION-398](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-398.md) and [QUESTION-399](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-399.md) call
    "The assistant's synthesis". It is Arm A's eleventh row (score 12) and
    was not shortlisted; it is the first candidate for the next review.
  - **The Arm B rows below the shortlist**, which were not reached:
    [QUESTION-380](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-380.md), [QUESTION-395](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-395.md), [QUESTION-374](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-374.md) and the smaller
    nucleating-argument clusters.
- **By-products, not filed, for the owner:**
  - A coboundary result on [CLAIM-537](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-537.md), as a candidate CLAIM in a
    contribution of its own: in [CLAIM-537](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-537.md)'s model, which configuration can
    be selected depends on each edge's range of disturbance within what the
    agent cannot tell apart, and only whether one exists depends on the
    disturbance's class in H¹. So reading the class exactly does not enable
    selection.
  - A candidate QUESTION from B5: does the self-model that makes a regime
    felt also present its owner?

## What the current-account view now shows

Seven syntheses, all Proposed, none Current, so no line has a current
account yet. Counting Proposed entries, the lines covered are:

- distributed-agency (six);
- will-organization (five);
- formal-apparatus ([SYNTHESIS-008](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-008.md));
- realizability ([SYNTHESIS-003](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-003.md));
- pragmatic-transport ([SYNTHESIS-005](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-005.md)).

**Still without a synthesis:**

- nucleating-argument, evidence-for-experience and readiness, where this
  review found the integrations already held as claims, or none;
- learned-structure, not reached;
- organizational-affect and authenticity, set aside.

The second synthesis review, at the owner's request, under [ADR-078](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-078.md) and the
`synthesis-review` skill. It is stacked on the derived-converses change
([ADR-079](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-079.md)), so what it files stores each relation on one side only. Four
read-only readers audited the shortlist, three candidates each, and checked
every quote of six words or more mechanically (71 in all, every one
matching). They reran the mathematics. The filer checked the admitted drafts
against the entries and corrected one: the readiness draft's illustrative
value model was the reader's own, not [CLAIM-561](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-561.md)'s, and is filed as
stipulated. The readers' reports were saved from their messages to the
session's scratchpad.

## The ranking

`scratch/formal/synthesis_candidates.py` found 628 claims, 568 in force, and

**The admitted, in brief.**

- **[SYNTHESIS-010](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-010.md) (from [CLAIM-600](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md)).** The case is a village water
  scheme that meets every condition, judged before withdrawal. It fails
  once the field officer whose visits kept contributions common knowledge
  is withdrawn. Two corrections are marked:
  - the conditions are judged, and standing inputs named, before
    withdrawal, which closes a free parameter;
  - the defeater's clause on the length of substitutive support, which the
    title dropped on 2026-11-05, is removed.

  It moved as Current under [ADR-077](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-077.md), since the claim was Active and its
  four premises are Active.
- **[SYNTHESIS-011](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-011.md) (from [CLAIM-336](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-336.md)).** The defeater's second clause is
  narrowed to the held-out test of matched complexity that A55 §7 gave and
  [ARG-065](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-065.md) holds. The case is one where transport observables are fixed by
  the receiver's state at reading time. The thesis stays the owner's.
- **[SYNTHESIS-009](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-009.md) ([QUESTION-395](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-395.md)).** Records kept per capacity fix only
  the marginals of [CLAIM-587](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-587.md)'s conjunction, so they bound readiness by the
  Fréchet inequalities. A refutation from the weakest capacity survives
  decay ([CLAIM-558](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-558.md)); a certification does not. Its bounds are textbook. The
  criterion and the asymmetry are new, and the reader flagged that a filer
  could fairly have filed it as a derived claim instead. With
  [SYNTHESIS-010](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-010.md), it gives the readiness line its first syntheses.

## Found along the way, for the owner

- **[CLAIM-404](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-404.md)** quotes [CLAIM-348](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-348.md)'s version-3 wording, "cannot be justified
  by the description that preserves it". [CLAIM-348](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-348.md) narrowed it on
  2026-10-29 to "cannot be justified solely by".
- **[CLAIM-572](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-572.md)'s summary** says greedy stopping misses the least total "in
  about a quarter of random systems". The rate depends on the generator:
  the reader's gave about half. "Of the random systems checked" would be
  exact.
- **[CLAIM-401](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-401.md):**
  - its citation of [THEORY-752](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-752.md) reads more than the reading shows;
    [QUESTION-222](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-222.md) carries the projection-relativity;
  - its dynamical-independence cell rests on [THEORY-820](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-820.md) and [THEORY-733](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-733.md),
    which are in neither its `grounds` nor its `rests_on`.
- **[CLAIM-425](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-425.md)** calls itself "the same achievement" as [CLAIM-424](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-424.md), but its
  title never requires revising standards. Either the title gains that, or
  the body says "the analogous regulation".
- **By-products, not filed:**
  - a demonstrated corollary of [CLAIM-366](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-366.md), answering part of [QUESTION-127](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-127.md).
    Common descent is constant on the orbits of every function-preserving
    symmetry that is a diffeomorphism of the parameters. A test with a
    fixed Euclidean budget is not: with f = v·relu(ux) and a rescaling by
    one half, the squared gradient norm is 612 at (4, 1) and 288 at its
    image (2, 2);
  - on [CASE-206](../../record/cases.d/CASE-206.md)'s vertex, a non-trivial agreement between outside and
    inside needs a shared budget of 4.125. That is more than the cheapest
    readiness (1.866) and more than full observation (4);
  - UFI is monotone in the actuator set, so it cannot be [QUESTION-380](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-380.md)'s
    predictor where adding a nucleus can hurt.

## What this round found

- **Nucleating-argument's integrations are held as claims.** All three of
  its `complements` clusters have now been audited across the three
  rounds, and so has its open question [QUESTION-038](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-038.md). Each integration is
  stated by a component's own body or notes. The line having no synthesis
  is a finding, as [ADR-078](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-078.md) allows, not a gap to fill.
- **Moving a claim that has objections would strand them.** A claim's
  `objects_to` accepts only CLAIMs, and SYNTHESIS has no `objected_by`.
  None of the nine claims moved so far has an objection, so nothing is
  stranded now. A move of [CLAIM-191](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-191.md) would strand [CLAIM-189](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-189.md), and a move of
  [CLAIM-440](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-440.md) would strand five. Like `rests_on` ([ADR-080](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-080.md)), the fix is
  probably a pattern for the `dialectic` chain. It should be decided with
  the first move that needs it, as that decision's demonstration.

Three further readiness links were found already stated, in [CASE-200](../../record/cases.d/CASE-200.md),
[CLAIM-572](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-572.md) and [TERM-112](../../record/terms.d/TERM-112.md).

**[CLAIM-633](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-633.md)'s derivation.** [CLAIM-524](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-524.md)'s network computes u₁v₁ + u₂v₂ with
resource ½ Σ(uᵢ + vᵢ). By AM–GM the resource is at least √(1 − p) + √p,
where p = u₂v₂, and that bound peaks at √2 when p = ½. A budget below √2
therefore splits the zero-loss set into a piece near p = 0 and a piece
near p = 1. Swapping the paths sends p to 1 − p and keeps the resource.
Each piece retracts to its endpoint without the resource rising: first
along a hyperbola to its balanced point, then along balanced points. No
entry names the swap, the orbit or the exchange. [CLAIM-263](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-263.md)'s step 1
quotients the full symmetry group. The claim is Proposed, and its
wording is the assistant's.

**Arm A.** No claim on either line only maps its components. [CLAIM-600](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md),
[CLAIM-632](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-632.md) and [CLAIM-620](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-620.md) have "Admission" sections, and their premises have
not changed in content. [CLAIM-556](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-556.md) adds an ordering and two repairs. Its
regeneration repair is close to a free parameter, which is flagged for
the owner.

**[CLAIM-600](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md)'s admission case meets its own defeater.** The village water
scheme in its "Admission" section was offered as a stipulated case
separating the claim from its premises. It could plainly occur. As
written, it meets the first clause of [CLAIM-600](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md)'s `defeated_if`: every
condition is judged met before withdrawal, and the scheme declines within
one turnover. When [CLAIM-600](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md) was an admitted synthesis, the case showed only
separation. Since [ADR-084](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-084.md) it is a claim again, and the skill's step for a
realistic separating case applies: the case is possible evidence against
the claim. [SYNTHESIS-032](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-032.md) lists it under "Not stated on the record".
The claim is unchanged, and its status is for the owner.

The sixth synthesis review, at the owner's request, run in parallel with
the defect sweep of the fifth round. It covered the next two smallest
lines with no account, realizability (122 entries when it began) and
will-organization (209). The owner asked during the round why the rounds
went from the smallest line up. The answer was that this was a choice of
cost and nothing more, and that the largest lines carry most of the
argument and most of the splits. The rounds after this one start from
distributed-agency.

Two read-only readers each drafted one line, with the briefs of the fifth
round, and then revised their drafts after the sweep (dmarx/nucleation#456),
the rulings on [CLAIM-600](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md) and [CLAIM-632](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-632.md) ([#457](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/457)), and the move below
([#458](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/458)) had changed what they covered. The filer then:

- checked coverage and quotes mechanically;
- reran `line_parts.py` on the filed parts;
- removed the two Superseded syntheses the realizability drafts had
  integrated, as the earlier accounts do;
- recounted the parts once the withdrawal inquiry had left.

## The ranking

Stage 1 was not rerun. The fifth round's ranking stands, and the
lines were chosen by size.

## The withdrawal inquiry, found again

The realizability reader's first draft had five parts. One was the
withdrawal part that [ADR-087](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-087.md) had moved to transient-support, mostly closed
inside realizability: 51 stored relations inside, 5 out and 2 in. Its
entries carried realizability because they bear on [QUESTION-398](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-398.md) or
[QUESTION-399](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-399.md), whose first line was realizability. Under [ADR-085](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-085.md) an entry
takes the first line of the question it bears on.

[ADR-088](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-088.md) (dmarx/nucleation#458) gives both questions, and the entries
that argue them, transient-support as their first line. It keeps
realizability on them only where a relation to a realizability-first
entry supplies it. None has one, so twenty-one entries leave
realizability. A first version kept [QUESTION-399](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-399.md) in realizability. The
recount showed the claims bearing on it closed off from the rest, with 14
stored relations inside and none out or in, so it moved too.
Transient-support's account, [SYNTHESIS-032](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-032.md), now integrates the five new
members.

**[CLAIM-600](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md)'s new admission case is realistic.** The ruling of
2026-11-11 ([#457](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/457)) narrowed [CLAIM-600](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md) to necessary conditions. Its new
admission case is a reintroduced population that persists through the
refuges it has reached after fire suppression is withdrawn while the fire
regime persists. The case separates the narrower claim from its premises,
and the claim says so. The realizability reader points out that the case
is realistic: refugia are common in fire ecology, and a case of that kind
meets the first clause of the claim's own `defeated_if`. Under [ADR-084](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-084.md)
that counts as evidence against the necessity of the threat condition. It
is a weaker form of the water scheme's problem, because no actual case is
cited. The condition probably needs restating as "the party no longer
needs the support against the threat". That restating risks a free
parameter, so it is left for the owner, not made here.

The seventh synthesis review, at the owner's request, and the first to
take the lines from the largest down. It covered distributed-agency, the
largest line with no account: 495 in-force entries when it began.

## How it ran

A Louvain community map of the line (stored relations weighted 2,
mentions 1) gave seven parts and 21 entries it left on their own. Seven
read-only readers each took one part, under one brief, and drafted its
account, its links to the other parts, and Arm A and Arm B. The filer
then:

- checked every quote of six words or more mechanically against the
  record, and checked by hand the ones the checker missed: nested quotes
  rendered with single quotes, and two quotes with elisions whose
  fragments run across line breaks;
- checked coverage: the part accounts and the line account together
  integrate every entry whose `line` includes distributed-agency,
  except [CASE-028](../../record/cases.d/CASE-028.md), Superseded by [CASE-006](../../record/cases.d/CASE-006.md);
- replaced the drafts' pointers to one another ("drafted beside this
  one") with the accounts' codes;
- wrote the line account over the parts.

## Filed

The line account, [SYNTHESIS-049](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-049.md), over ten part accounts:

- conferral and authority, [SYNTHESIS-050](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-050.md) (99 entries);
- availability before a deadline, [SYNTHESIS-057](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-057.md) (21);
- partners coming to depend on one another, [SYNTHESIS-053](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-053.md) (11);
- perspectives, legibility and correction, [SYNTHESIS-056](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-056.md) (63);
- the unit of a combined form, [SYNTHESIS-054](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-054.md) (81);
- individuation, [SYNTHESIS-048](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-048.md) (71);
- frustration, [SYNTHESIS-051](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-051.md) (53, with the claim below);
- persistence, [SYNTHESIS-047](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-047.md) (40);
- world-modeling, [SYNTHESIS-055](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-055.md) (6);
- collective stance, [SYNTHESIS-052](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-052.md) (29).

The line account integrates 21 entries directly: the selflessness group
([CLAIM-491](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-491.md) and its objections and questions), [CLAIM-045](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-045.md) with [CLAIM-110](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-110.md),
[QUESTION-365](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-365.md), and the ten questions below that link to nothing in the
line.

## Three parts that were three inquiries

The map's parts are not always one inquiry each. Read through:

- **Normative-institutional (95) was three.** Availability before a
  deadline (21 entries: 41 linked pairs inside, 12 to the rest of the
  map's part, 1 to the rest of the line), partners coming to depend on one
  another (11: 15 inside, 3 to the rest of the part, all through [CLAIM-060](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-060.md),
  2 to the line) and perspectives, legibility and correction (63). Each has
  its own account.
- **Persistence (47) held world-modeling.** Six entries with 12 linked
  pairs among them and 2 to the other 41, both through [TERM-086](../../record/terms.d/TERM-086.md). The
  reader also named a third candidate, seven entries on identifying
  perspectives (13 pairs inside, 6 out), and kept it in the main account.
- **The other five parts held together.**

Counted over the whole line rather than the map's part, availability and
dependence are no more closed than the larger parts: about one pair in
four crosses, against one in three for conferral. So neither is proposed
as a line of its own. The line account gives the counts.

## Claims

- **Filed (Arm B, derivation): [CLAIM-634](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-634.md).** For [CLAIM-538](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-538.md)'s demands
  on offsets between contexts, |x_v − x_u − a_e| ≤ δ_e, the minimal
  non-faces of [CLAIM-347](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md)'s compatibility complex are exactly the simple
  cycles whose holonomy exceeds their summed tolerance. It is the standard
  result on systems of difference constraints (a system is infeasible
  exactly when its constraint graph has a negative cycle), and the
  filer checked the reduction. [CLAIM-538](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-538.md) disclaims the general link to
  [CLAIM-347](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md)'s complex, and no entry states it for this class. The
  frustration account integrates it.
- **No other Arm B link passed.** Each reader tested several sentences, and
  each failed by a separating case, a free parameter, or because an entry
  already states it. The line account lists four more tested across
  parts. The one the owner may want to see is the last of them: whether
  the unit's lasting ([CLAIM-157](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-157.md)) is what persistence by transmission
  ([CLAIM-615](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-615.md)) measures turns on what makes a later block "that block",
  which neither says.
- **Arm A: no claim in the line only maps its components.** [CLAIM-622](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-622.md)
  (one premise) is thin and its `defeated_if` already names restatement.
  [CLAIM-348](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-348.md) adds an anti-circularity clause, and a stipulated case
  separates it; it has no "Admission" section, and could take that case.

## For the owner

- **[CLAIM-615](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-615.md)'s admission case is realistic.** A mechanism passed to an
  unrelated workshop and counted the same by continuity of its parts (a
  car that changes garages) is almost word for word the second clause of
  its own `defeated_if`. It defeats the claim unless "the relations that
  keep its repertoire realizable" is read as the object's internal
  organization, and its fourth layer lets that organization lie outside
  the individual. The slot needs closing.
- **[CLAIM-342](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-342.md)'s term is open.** Authority that reinforces itself without
  passing through any interpretation, held against independent evidence
  too weak to overturn it ([CLAIM-408](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-408.md)'s normal form with a tilt below
  critical; Arthur's increasing returns), meets [CLAIM-342](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-342.md)'s `defeated_if`
  if share-dependent advantage counts as independent scoring, and not if
  it counts as scoring that passes through what the loop tests. [CASE-155](../../record/cases.d/CASE-155.md)
  frames the term as scoring "that depends on who governs"; [CLAIM-342](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-342.md) says
  "interpretation".
- **[CLAIM-613](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-613.md)'s `defeated_if`** can be met by one documented ordinary
  fork, which is easy for an existence claim.
- **Ten questions carry the line and link to nothing in it**:

The eighth synthesis review, at the owner's request, run while the
seventh's pull request (dmarx/nucleation#461) waited on CI. It covered
pragmatic-transport, the next largest line with no account: 391 in-force
entries when it began.

## How it ran

As in the seventh round: a Louvain community map of the line (stored
relations weighted 2, mentions 1, resolution 0.7) gave eight parts and
eleven entries it left on their own, and eight read-only readers each
drafted one part under one brief. A usage limit stopped all eight midway;
each resumed from its saved files once it lifted. The filer then checked
coverage mechanically (every in-force entry of the line integrated, once),
replaced the drafts' file pointers with codes, checked the four drafted
claims' derivations, added inactive-ok lines the drafts lacked for
Answered questions, and wrote the line account.

Three entries moved between the map's parts on reading: [CLAIM-257](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-257.md) from
contextuality to fidelity, [TERM-011](../../record/terms.d/TERM-011.md) from fidelity to frames, and
[QUESTION-024](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-024.md) from contextuality to the study part.

## Filed

The line account, [SYNTHESIS-066](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-066.md), over twelve part accounts:

- communicative kinds, [SYNTHESIS-068](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-068.md) (78 entries);
- fidelity relative to receivers, [SYNTHESIS-064](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-064.md) (77);
- the communicative object, [SYNTHESIS-069](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-069.md) (57);
- what the line adds and how it is tested, [SYNTHESIS-070](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-070.md) (24);
- language models as a test bed, [SYNTHESIS-059](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-059.md) (8);
- composition in conditional generation, [SYNTHESIS-061](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-061.md) (9);
- directed transport by kernels, [SYNTHESIS-063](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-063.md) (40);
- the act a rendering keeps, [SYNTHESIS-058](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-058.md) (27);
- Saussure's value, [SYNTHESIS-065](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-065.md) (7);
- frames and the judgement–observation loop, [SYNTHESIS-062](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-062.md) (34);
- reconstruction chains, [SYNTHESIS-067](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-067.md) (17);
- conservation under kernels, [SYNTHESIS-060](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-060.md) (6).

Three of the map's parts were more than one inquiry: study fell into
three (4 linked pairs between them), act held a cluster on Saussure's
value joined by one pair, and chains held five entries on conservation
joined by two. The others held together.

## Claims filed (Arm B, derivation)

The filer checked each derivation.

- **[CLAIM-635](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-635.md)** (chains reader). If every kernel leaves f fixed,
  E[g(S_n) | S_0] = g(S_0) for g = f − E f(S_0); the test function
  sgn(g(x))·g(y) has mean E|g| under the joint law and 0 under the product,
  and is bounded by ‖g‖∞, so total variation is at least E|g|/(2‖g‖∞), and
  Pinsker gives I(S_0; S_n) ≥ (E|g|)²/(2‖g‖∞²) for every n.
- **[CLAIM-637](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-637.md)** (kernels reader). Within a context, one kernel
  fitting every item exactly is the definition of a garbling, and a
  constant target is fitted by the constant kernel. So the restated D_obs
  and its Le Cam deficiency charge a rendering for what it adds about the
  item and nothing for what it loses. This bears on [CLAIM-228](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-228.md)'s thesis
  that the restated measure separates what recovery separates: a
  procedure and its collapse are separated by recovery and not by the
  measure.
- **[CLAIM-638](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-638.md)** (kernels reader). Triangle inequality and data
  processing under one kernel: a rendering's order effect exceeds the
  source's by at most the two order-context distortions. A permutation
  example shows kernels fitted per order bound nothing.
- **[CLAIM-636](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-636.md)** (fidelity reader). Where a literal rendering is
  Blackwell-equivalent to the source on the declared problems, any
  rendering made from the source alone is a garbling of it, so it is
  never the better report for an ideal receiver; [CLAIM-461](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-461.md)'s objection is
  then a gain in usable information under the readers' code ([CLAIM-199](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-199.md)).

Each says in its "Admission" section that it is a short composition;
whether that is enough to keep it is the owner's call.

No other Arm B link passed: the readers tested about forty, which failed
by separating cases, free parameters, or because an entry already states
them, and the line account lists three more tested across parts. Arm A
found no claim that only maps its components. The nearest were [CLAIM-204](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-204.md)
(it calls itself "the integrative statement" but carries two defeat
disjuncts no component does), [CLAIM-129](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-129.md) and [CLAIM-081](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-081.md) (which have no
"Admission" sections and could take the separating cases the readers
built), and [CLAIM-342](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-342.md), which passes by a separating case.

The ninth synthesis review, at the owner's request ("proceed"), the last
of the large lines with no account: formal-apparatus, 234 in-force
entries when it began.

## How it ran

The line is unlike the others. Most of its entries are first in another
line, and its relations are sparse: a Louvain map (stored relations
weighted 2, mentions 1, resolution 0.7) found seven parts of 9 to 38
entries, eleven small clusters of two to six with no link to the rest,
and 46 entries linked to no other entry of the line. Nine read-only
readers took the seven parts, the clusters together and the unlinked
entries together, under one brief that added a note on the line's shape.
The filer then checked coverage (every in-force entry integrated once),
replaced the readers' working labels ("part-1", "cluster 2") with the
accounts' codes, checked the three drafted claims' derivations, dropped
one drafted account (below) and wrote the line account.

## Filed

The line account, [SYNTHESIS-088](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-088.md), over eighteen part accounts:

- reaching under a budget, [SYNTHESIS-076](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-076.md) (39 entries, with
  [CLAIM-639](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-639.md));
- effective descriptions, [SYNTHESIS-075](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-075.md) (27);
- interventions and closure, [SYNTHESIS-079](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-079.md) (20);

- joint satisfiability, [SYNTHESIS-074](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-074.md) (19);
- gluing, [SYNTHESIS-082](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-082.md) (17);

- stability against persistence, [SYNTHESIS-080](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-080.md) (10, with
  [CLAIM-640](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-640.md));
- from the small clusters: conservation, [SYNTHESIS-071](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-071.md) (6); Granger

replaced by the accounts' codes (version 2 of each).

## Claims filed (Arm B, derivation)

The filer checked each derivation.

- **[CLAIM-639](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-639.md)** (reachability reader): knowing each requirement to
  within ε fixes every threshold to within ε ([CLAIM-580](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-580.md)), but two merges
  of [CLAIM-592](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-592.md)'s merge tree within 2ε of each other can be reordered, so
  which levels an observer's partitions agree with is not fixed. It
  qualifies [CLAIM-592](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-592.md)'s design lever.
- **[CLAIM-640](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-640.md)** (stability reader): with symmetric exchange among
  viable regimes, the restricted generator is L + E with 0 ≤ E ≤ ε, so by
  Weyl's inequality the survivors' relaxation rate is within ε of the
  exchange Laplacian's gap, and the separation between settling and dying
  out goes as 4k/ε for two regimes, π²k/(nε) for a line and n²k/ε for a
  complete graph. Textbook mathematics; it joins the stability part's two
  strands.
- **[CLAIM-641](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-641.md)** (unlinked reader): the kernel w(u,v)/√(w(u)w(v)) is
  [CLAIM-370](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-370.md)'s conditional-expectation operator carried by the unitary
  multiplication by √w, so the two have one spectrum and the kernel's
  squared norm is 1 + χ².

Each is short; whether that is enough to keep it is the owner's call. No
other Arm B sentence passed; the readers tested about fifty.

## Reading review of 2026-11-11, by line: normative judgment about organizations; 55 readings named, four tied, one question raised, fifty held; the view does not count readings a claim or argument grounds on

*2026-11-11 07:21:41*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: ADR-091 ADR-090 — Proposed; the decisions this review runs under, filed with it -->
<!-- inactive-ok-file: SYNTHESIS-038 CLAIM-619 CLAIM-624 CLAIM-445 CLAIM-364 CLAIM-192 CLAIM-271 CLAIM-603 ARG-043 ARG-062 — Proposed; the line's account and entries cited as they stand, with their standing -->
<!-- inactive-ok-file: THEORY-040 THEORY-071 THEORY-1285 — Proposed; the accounts the Active readings are split from, and a reading outside the view because it is not in force -->

The first reading review, run under [ADR-091](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-091.md) as its demonstration, in
the by-line mode, on organizational-normativity: the line the view of
readings by line ([ADR-090](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-090.md)) showed using no reading. The line's
account is [SYNTHESIS-038](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-038.md). Its question for this run: what should this line
be building on, and is not?

## The list

The view was rendered locally from record/views.d/readings-by-line.md.j2,
since docs/readings-by-line.md is not yet generated. It named 579 readings
in force that no line uses. From them the review took:

- **by topic:** the 47 with any of the topics `ethics`, `self-governance`,
  `social-ontology`, `moral-psychology` or `society-and-governance` (the
  line's account carries the first, second and fifth; the others are the
  vocabulary's words for the rest of the line's subject), in any position,
  not only first; `altruism`, `future-generations` and `social-identity`
  found none;
- **by question:** none. No unused reading has `bears_on` or `answers` to
  the line's questions, [QUESTION-128](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-128.md), [QUESTION-129](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-129.md), [QUESTION-256](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-256.md) and
  [QUESTION-441](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-441.md);
- **by text:** a search of the 579 for the line's terms (answerability,
  accountability, legitimacy, correctability, corrigibility,
  responsibility, normativity, obligation, duty, blame, wrong, unjust,
  institution, organization, governance, moral), title hits first, then
  the files with the most hits. Most hits are false (harmonic analysis,
  "institutions" in the logical sense, tags). Eight were added whose
  content might meet the line: [THEORY-1119](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1119.md), [THEORY-1306](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1306.md), [THEORY-1335](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1335.md),
  [THEORY-835](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-835.md), [THEORY-636](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-636.md), [THEORY-1117](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1117.md), [THEORY-404](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-404.md) and [THEORY-1289](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1289.md).

55 readings in all, each read in full, with its source and its relations.
The line's entries were read against them: the claims, questions, term
and arguments [SYNTHESIS-038](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-038.md) integrates, with [CLAIM-462](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-462.md), [CLAIM-523](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-523.md),
[CLAIM-445](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-445.md), [CLAIM-348](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-348.md) and [TERM-100](../../record/terms.d/TERM-100.md), which those entries rest on or use.

**A defect in the view, found in stage 1.** 19 of the 55 are not unused.
In force claims or arguments ground on them, and the view does not see
it. The template reads a reading's uses from `t.supports`, the converse of
`grounds`, and from `t.reports`, the converse of `reported_in`. Both are
derived fields that no file stores, and under `views.render` both come
back empty for every reading ([THEORY-140](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-140.md)'s `supports` is empty though
[CLAIM-619](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-619.md) and [ARG-062](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-062.md) ground on it; so is [THEORY-911](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-911.md)'s, though [CLAIM-445](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-445.md)
grounds on it). The view therefore counts only `corroborates`, `answers`
and `bears_on`. Across the record, 129 of the 579 readings it calls
unused are grounded on by a claim or argument not retired, most of
those uses in distributed-agency and pragmatic-transport by first line. This line
is not at zero either: [CLAIM-619](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-619.md) and [ARG-062](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-062.md) ground on [THEORY-140](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-140.md), which
is in force ([ARG-043](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-043.md) grounds on [THEORY-1285](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1285.md), which is Proposed and so
outside the view). The 19 were reviewed all the same, against this
line, since none of their uses is in it. The fix is the template's, not
this review's: derive the users from the claims and arguments
(`docs("CLAIM")`, `docs("ARG")`, and CASE's `reported_in`) rather than
from the converse fields.

## Verdicts

### Tied (4)

- **[THEORY-1119](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1119.md)** (Barandiaran, Di Paolo and Rohde) `bears_on`
  [QUESTION-128](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-128.md). The question asks whether "norms of function and failure
  [can] be defined from an organization's own dynamics", and its body
  cites the work, through [THEORY-071](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-071.md) (Proposed), for "Self-generated
  normativity as a condition of agency". [THEORY-1119](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1119.md) is the Active
  reading of what the paper proposes. Also grounded by [CLAIM-284](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-284.md),
  [CLAIM-194](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-194.md) and [CLAIM-288](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-288.md) (distributed-agency).
- **[THEORY-1165](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1165.md)** (Kahl) `bears_on` [QUESTION-441](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-441.md). Its third part asks
  when the counter-normativity is "the organization's own rather than its
  participants' or an outside maintainer's"; Kahl's criterion is
  "whether revision of that rule under breakdown is internal or external
  to the candidate group agent", and institutional systems fail it
  because their standards are "authored elsewhere". Also `bears_on` the
  question raised below. Also grounded by [CLAIM-485](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-485.md) (distributed-agency).
- **[THEORY-1463](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1463.md)** (Pritchett, Woolcock and Andrews) `bears_on`
  [QUESTION-441](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-441.md), which asks what makes reproductive the counter-normativity
  of an organization that "reproduces the representational projections
  that make the harm non-legible". Isomorphic mimicry is "keeping
  legitimacy by imitating the forms of functional organizations without
  their function", with de jure scores above de facto ones. The authors
  offer it as how failure persists, untested against alternatives, and
  the harm is a capability failure; the history note says so.
- **[THEORY-837](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-837.md)** (Besley and Prat) `corroborates` [CLAIM-462](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-462.md), that an
  arrangement "can keep, or increase, its capacity for effective action
  while its capacity to be effectively corrected by others degrades,
  because the two are maintained by different relations". Under capture
  the incumbent keeps office and voters "never remove a bad incumbent";
  the relation degraded, the outlets' report, is one the incumbent's
  action does not need. [CLAIM-462](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-462.md) is distributed-agency's, and a premise
  of [CLAIM-624](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-624.md) in this line. The model is one-shot, so it is not tied to

  also ties [THEORY-1118](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1118.md) to [QUESTION-071](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-071.md) (will-organization), whose summary
  cites [THEORY-040](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-040.md) (Proposed) for the same argument; [THEORY-1118](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1118.md) is its

## A self-reproducing compiler Trojan horse filed as a case for the question of installed counter-normativity: Thompson's lecture and Stute's story, read

*2026-11-11 07:44:10*

<!-- inactive-ok-file: THEORY-1560 THEORY-1561 — Proposed; the readings filed with this entry, cited with their standing -->

The owner offered Stute's Quora answer, republished by Forbes, as a case
for [QUESTION-449](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-449.md), and pasted its text when the pages refused a fetch.

## Where the record already held it

Nothing. The record held no entry on compiler Trojan horses,
self-reproducing programs or Thompson's lecture; [NOTE-099](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-099.md) mentions a
compiler only as a translating level of abstraction. The question it was
offered for, [QUESTION-449](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-449.md), and the term it turns on, [TERM-100](../../record/terms.d/TERM-100.md)
(formation against maintenance provenance), are held, as is [CLAIM-522](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md) on
interventions on state against interventions on production.

## What was filed

- **Stute's answer**: [LIT-2331](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2331.md), read from the owner's copy (Forbes and
  Quora returned HTTP 403 to a fetch on 2026-11-11), [NOTE-1714](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1714.md), and
  [THEORY-1561](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1561.md), Proposed.
- **Thompson's lecture**, the documented original of the mechanism the
  story tells: [LIT-2332](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2332.md) (doi:10.1145/358198.358210, checked against
  Crossref), read in full from a course copy (d.umn.edu), [NOTE-1715](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1715.md),
  and [THEORY-1560](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1560.md), Proposed.
- **[CASE-232](../../record/cases.d/CASE-232.md)**, standing `stipulated`, kind `specimen`: the story as a
  case, reported in [THEORY-1561](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1561.md), illustrating [CLAIM-522](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md), in
  organizational-normativity (for the question) and distributed-agency
  (for [CLAIM-522](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md)).
- **Dated notes** on [QUESTION-449](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-449.md) (version 2) and [CLAIM-522](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md) (version 4).
- Both readings `bears_on` [QUESTION-449](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-449.md). The case itself cannot: no
  field takes a case to a question, the gap raised with the owner the same
  day.

## What the case adds, and what it does not

The case separates two readings of the question's "whose process now
maintains it": a host's routine that carries a mechanism, and an installed
component that maintains itself by running inside that routine, hidden
from the host. The story is of the second kind, so it does not reach an
organization that reproduces a mechanism it can see. The reading is the
assistant's, offered in the notes and not filed as a claim.

## What was left, and why

- The story's details (the 3B2, the AT&T technician, the Tymnet access)
  are kept in the NOTE and the case, not filed: they bear on nothing.
- The Air Force critique of Multics that Thompson credits is not
  registered: he could not cite it, and no reference was sought.
- No ARG: the case `illustrates` [CLAIM-522](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md) and says it bears none of its
  weight; nothing filed argues support.
- No topic fits computer security; both works are tagged `epistemology`,
  for Thompson's question of trust in code one did not write.

the entries' own text.

## The moved conditions

The readers found that a question holding a reading's former
`promote_when` ([ADR-065](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md)) usually had no relation from that reading: the
move wrote the question and not the tie. Of 129 questions that name their
parent reading, 95 lacked it. The readers wrote some; the filer wrote the
remaining 73, each `bears_on` from the reading, with a history note quoting
the question's own words. The skill now says the move writes it.

## Flags, not fixed

- **[QUESTION-423](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-423.md) may be answered in part** ([ADR-049](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md)): its note of
  2026-11-06 says every clause but Theorem 2 has its independent
  computation, and [CLAIM-609](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-609.md) now bears on it.
- **Stale "answer it in part"** in [QUESTION-048](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-048.md), [QUESTION-062](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-062.md) and
  [QUESTION-066](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-066.md), whose readings bear on them.
- **[QUESTION-091](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-091.md)** cites the Superseded [CLAIM-163](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-163.md) as a live objection.
- **Lines given by default**: [QUESTION-187](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-187.md) and [QUESTION-352](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-352.md), on
  distributed-agency (as the line's account already says).
- **Template comments** left in [QUESTION-201](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-201.md) and [QUESTION-228](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-228.md).
- **[QUESTION-050](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-050.md)** waits on the owner: whether [CLAIM-204](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-204.md), [CLAIM-223](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-223.md) and
  four cases answer it.
- **[ARG-051](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-051.md) bears on [QUESTION-367](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-367.md)**, but an argument has no `bears_on`.

## The skill

Revised from the run: a moved condition's reading bears on its question;
whose words count for a tie; a question that tests a claim takes no
relation from it; a claim that names a question only to set it aside takes
none; Proposed readings may be tied; a split run writes one curation entry.

The fourth run of the reading review ([ADR-091](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-091.md)), and its first in the

by-question passes were done; this run takes the largest primary topics

use it.

representation-learning (49); mathematics (45); quantum-foundations with
contextuality, logic, compositionality and philosophy-of-mathematics
(37); probabilistic-modeling with information-theory, information-geometry

conflict: two parts each changed [CLAIM-543](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-543.md)'s grounds, and both changes
stand as successive versions.

| mathematics | 9 | 3 | 33 | 0 |

Every tie quotes the tied entry's own words in the reading's history (or

a question's named instruments count as use (they read them as
`corroborates` and `bears_on`); how to count a reading tied to several
entries (once); that two parts of a split run should check each other's
raises; and that a case's or term's citation of a reading is use the
schemes cannot record. These are for a revision of the skill.

## What the skill does not yet say

The readers met these, and answered them the same way:

- **A reading a claim cites only as a limit, a caution or a bound on its
  scope** (in "What it does not say") takes no relation: no relation runs
  from a reading to a claim it bounds. Such readings will keep showing as
  unused. [ADR-093](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-093.md) gives questions their cautions (`bears_on`), not
  claims.
- **A question that names a reading only as a "neighbour"** does not name
  it as evidence.
- **A link a claim itself calls an analogy** from another domain falls
  under the scope test and takes nothing.
- **A work with two readings**: the one whose content the entry's words use
  takes the relation.

Whether a claim's limits and cautions should have a relation of their own
is the one that changes what the view can show; it is for a decision.

The readers met the same near cases, and the decision's point 2 now
settles them: a reading that holds what the claim leaves out ("that is
THEORY-n's question") bounds it; a reading given as the reason for a
disclaimer bounds it; a reading weighed as a position, named as the
defeater or placed as prior art does not; the words decide where a limit
also supports the headline.

## For whoever runs parallel readers next

Use a unique scratch file name per reader; one reader read another's file
by name. `luria relate` reads standard input, so it is not run inside a
`while read` loop without `</dev/null`.

On 2026-11-12 the owner asked for the exchange "Identify Synthesis
Opportunities" (https://chatgpt.com/share/6af51819-4de8-83ea-b5aa-5edc65869c44,
2026-11-08 20:58 to 22:29 UTC, owner turns U1 to U8) to be read and filed.
The verbatim decoded text was the source throughout.

In U1 the owner asked A where SYNTHESIS entries, then a new scheme, were
needed. A surveyed the record (A3), then drafted accounts for six lines,
two new claims with their construction cases, an owner-supplied case and a
proposed study, as patch bundles in its own sandbox. A could not write to
the repository. A7: "The repository write requires an authorization step
that wasn't approved", and A22: "Nothing has been committed to GitHub."
The bundles are not in the export. So A's "filed" items are proposals,
known only from A's descriptions of them.

The filing followed the `read-and-file` skill ([ADR-068](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-068.md)). Its scope, set
by the lead: the full map against the record, the idea ledger, the
owner's ideas and those of A's that have content of their own and are not
held, ARGs where support is load-bearing or contested, dated notes, the

**Findings, by check.**

- **Attribution.** A3 to A22 are A's, and A credits the owner's U5
  instruction and U6 case as the owner's. A16 makes the case its own,
  "a documented practitioner" case; it is the owner's find, and its
  framing (compute on demand against learn and amortize) is the owner's
  U6, not A's. A18's history answers the owner's U7.
- **Coverage.** A's plan drops nothing the owner contributed. Its drafts
  covered 41 of 97 will-organization claims and 50 of 188
  distributed-agency claims by its own count, and none of pragmatic-transport
  or formal-apparatus; A said so (A22).
- **Fidelity.** A's descriptions of record entries check out (above).
  A16's claim that [CLAIM-303](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-303.md) "already states the upfront-cost-versus-reuse
  criterion" is right about [CLAIM-303](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-303.md)'s arithmetic. Its thesis is about
  filing arguments, so the case bears on [QUESTION-095](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-095.md) and illustrates no
  claim; A had it illustrate [CLAIM-303](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-303.md).
- **Standing.** A keeps its drafts Proposed and says lint and fidelity
  review are outstanding. A14 calls the construction cases `fictional`
  and `construction`, which they are.
- **Integration.** A18's integration is that improved reference
  conditioning moves the break-even toward computing on demand. As a
  conditional it is [CLAIM-303](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-303.md)'s arithmetic: a smaller per-use saving needs
  more uses. As a fact about model generations it is a discriminating
  prediction, but A declined to assert it ("measures that crossover rather
  than assuming its direction"), and the study is where the record holds
  it. No claim is filed.

No record account is revised. The entries filed here are Proposed, so
no account's coverage of in-force components changes. The next synthesis

## Left, and why

- **A's claim from the two-capacity construction** (A8: "Improving the
  success probability of every required capacity can decrease overall
  readiness if the dependencies between capacities change"). Held in
  substance by [CLAIM-632](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-632.md): per-capacity records identify readiness only
  when the dependence is known, and its certification rule, with the
  earlier upper bound as the floor, is the comparative form. A one-step
  application of an existing claim does not pass as a derivation that no
  claim holds. The construction is filed as a case, and [CLAIM-632](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-632.md) has a
  note. If the owner wants the comparative form as a claim of its own, it
  is ready in that note.
- **A's revision of [SYNTHESIS-015](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-015.md)** (A18) to integrate the two cases:
  not made. The cases bear on [QUESTION-095](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-095.md), which [SYNTHESIS-015](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-015.md) and
  [SYNTHESIS-057](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-057.md) integrate; whether the account takes them is the next
  review's call.
- **A's link from the case to [CLAIM-303](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-303.md) by `illustrates`** (A16, A18):
  not made, for the reason under "Fidelity".
- **Stable Diffusion 1.x and SDXL** in A18's table are model generations,
  not works A cites; not registered. **MiniMax H3** has no work to
  register; A's description of it as "primarily a video-generation model"

- **A18's citations** (`turn158340reddit12`, `turn218229academia48` to
  `50`, `turn428783search0` and `search3`) are tool references with no
  addresses in the export. The works were identified from A's prose.
- **A's coverage report, review notes and verification scripts**: in the

- **A's "What I would do first" and closing offers** (A3, A22): plans, now

On 2026-11-12 the lead filed the exchange "Meaning Transmission
Explained" (https://chatgpt.com/share/6af517f7-cb48-83ea-8395-df7d52333dc7,
2026-11-07, 18:59 to 20:16 UTC, five owner turns), one of the discussions
the owner asked to have read and filed. The decoded share was read
verbatim from the scratchpad. The filing followed the `read-and-file`
skill ([ADR-068](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-068.md)).

The owner asked at U1 for the record's "account of how meaning can be
transmitted independent of any sentient emitter or receiver". A3 relayed
it. At U2 the owner proposed a smoke detector that sets off sprinklers as
a toy model. At U3 the owner added a debugging case. A4, A5, A8 and A10
developed both, and A10 reported running a small Python model. U4 asked
for "additional points of contact with the Nucleation inquiry", and U5
said "proceed".

**Scope set by the lead.** The full map against the record, an idea
ledger, filing of the owner's ideas and of A's that have content of their
own and are not held, ARGs where support is load-bearing or contested,
dated notes, the synthesis audit, this entry and a changelog fragment. The
exchange names no work outside the record: every work it relies on is
held and read (Kolchinsky and Wolpert, [LIT-1149](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1149.md); Grice, [LIT-1042](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1042.md); the
Simondon readings, [LIT-1911](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1911.md) and [LIT-1922](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1922.md)). So nothing was registered, and
the owner supplied no link to read. No earlier filing of this share was
found; the lead found no match for its id, "smoke detector" or
"sprinkler".

- **Idea 1.** The record holds Grice's tests in [NOTE-735](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-735.md) and [THEORY-444](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-444.md),
  and nothing applying them to signals. [CASE-243](../../record/cases.d/CASE-243.md)'s body already
  separates the two meanings. The claim adds where the norm sits, and its
  defeater names the restatement objection.
- **Idea 2.** The forager construction was built and run with exact
  fractions:
  - the two profiles agree on a silent patch;
  - only the designer's flags a yield that falls to 1.5 but still pays;
  - only the self-set profile flags an upkeep risen to 3.5 past a yield of
    3, and the designer's forager dies at step 119.

  The construction is stipulated, so it shows that the two norms differ,
  not that a simulated one is owned. The claim's defeater says so.

  0.95, [CLAIM-632](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-632.md)'s bounds are 0.92 and 0.95, and the independent product
  0.92169 lies between them.

A selection-based teleosemantic account (Millikan) would bear on ideas 1
and 2. It is unread here, and both entries say the reading is owed.
