## Arguments

Every place the filing says one entry supports another, checked for
whether it is load-bearing or contested (step 10):

- [ARG-097](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-097.md) (formal-application, Proposed): [LIT-1213](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1213.md) to
  [CLAIM-668](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-668.md). Halpern and Moses's theorems apply once reading the
  record is receiving an unacknowledged message at an unbounded time; a
  team reading on a shared clock is outside them. Load-bearing: the
  claim's only ground.
- [ARG-096](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-096.md) (existence, Proposed): [CASE-131](../../record/cases.d/CASE-131.md) to [CLAIM-666](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-666.md). The case
  shows that preserving the graph fails as a criterion; the migration is a
  stipulated counterfactual, since the relation never merged; the positive
  criterion rests on [CLAIM-250](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-250.md), not on the case.
- No other support judgement is load-bearing or contested. [CLAIM-664](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-664.md)
  and [CLAIM-668](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-668.md) rest on held claims through `rests_on`. The notes'
  links of A's tests to held entries are illustrations, and A's readings of
  held entries were accurate (below), so none needed an ARG.

## Syntheses audited

The exchange has eight overall accounts. Two are the syntheses the owner
asked for (A45 at U19, A48 at U20); the others close a turn.

| synthesis | class | filed |
|---|---|---|
| A20 §7, A22 "proposed central argument", A25 "productive tension": luria as governed revision of its own terms | descriptive of the record-as-apparatus line, plus a novelty claim | recap; the novelty claim as [QUESTION-458](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-458.md) |
| A32 closing formulation, A34 "collective correctability" | proposed | recap; the testable part as [QUESTION-459](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-459.md) |
| A36 "overarching contribution" | proposed | recap |
| A39 "central hypothesis" | proposed | an earlier, broader version of [CLAIM-667](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-667.md) |
| A41 and A43 hypothesis on governed recursive improvement | proposed | [QUESTION-457](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-457.md) |
| A45, at U19 | proposed | [CLAIM-667](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-667.md) (§3); map in [SYNTHESIS-090](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-090.md) |
| A48, at U20 | proposed | no claim; its prediction kept in [CASE-254](../../record/cases.d/CASE-254.md) |
| A50 §15 | proposed | no claim |

**Integration, by thesis.**

- A20, A22 and A25 say luria revises not only knowledge but the commitments
  by which knowledge is recorded. That is [CLAIM-419](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-419.md), [CLAIM-195](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-195.md) and
  [SYNTHESIS-012](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-012.md). What they add is that this is luria's distinctive
  contribution, a comparison with prior art the record has not read: no
  route admits it, so it is a question.
- A34: luria as "infrastructure for collective correctability", a
  substrate for organizing "some of" the operations [TERM-085](../../record/terms.d/TERM-085.md) names. The
  free parameter "some" absorbs every case, so no separating case or
  prediction exists; recap.
- A36: a record "can change the conditions under which distributed
  contributions become legible, authoritative, actionable, and
  correctable". A possibility [CLAIM-419](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-419.md) already grants; recap.
- A39: a governed, extensible workspace "improves the collective
  correctability of distributed agents when failures require revising" its
  representations and procedures. A prediction, but a main effect of
  governance would confirm it without saying whether governance and
  modifiability interact. The narrower sentence, the interaction, passes
  and is [CLAIM-667](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-667.md).
- A41 and A43: improvements "accumulate across generations while
  preserving" correctability. A prediction with a stated outcome against
  it, but it is the expected answer to the owner's U17, nothing the
  record holds bears on its sign, and A frames it as "the most interesting
  hypothesis": filed as the question, with A's yes and no outcomes.
- A45: three integrations. Its six-concept "causal decomposition of
  collective learning and correction" is a map of [TERM-089](../../record/terms.d/TERM-089.md), [TERM-064](../../record/terms.d/TERM-064.md),
  [CLAIM-403](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-403.md), [TERM-085](../../record/terms.d/TERM-085.md), [CLAIM-470](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-470.md) and [CASE-186](../../record/cases.d/CASE-186.md); recap. Its levels of change,
  "nested but not automatically progressive", are a design caution carried
  into [CASE-253](../../record/cases.d/CASE-253.md). Its 2×2 interaction passes the discriminating-
  prediction route: [CLAIM-667](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-667.md). Its closing thesis, that an apparatus
  "can support cumulative improvement" and that whether it does "depends
  on" its capacities, is unfalsifiable as stated.
- A48: its "deeper synthesis", that a record's distinctions between what
  is known and assumed, expressible and not, endorsed and considered,
  changeable and authorized are "prerequisites for different kinds of
  correction", fails as stated by A45's own concession that a fixed-schema
  team "might still answer through careful prose". The narrower sentence
  is A48's "resource-bounded legibility" outcome, which A offers as a
  possible finding, not a thesis; it is kept in [CASE-254](../../record/cases.d/CASE-254.md) as the
  result the study would test, not filed as a claim.
- A50 §15: five problems "can arise in the same inquiry", shown by A45
  §4's four versions of [CASE-131](../../record/cases.d/CASE-131.md) (note on [CASE-131](../../record/cases.d/CASE-131.md)); the rest is a
  research question, carried by [QUESTION-459](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-459.md), [QUESTION-457](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-457.md) and
  [CASE-254](../../record/cases.d/CASE-254.md).

**Findings, by check.**

- **(a) Attribution.** A45 tells the program as "we" throughout ("We
  started with Luria as a flexible knowledge-record system"). The steering
  was the owner's: U8 is the centre of Study 2, which A45 calls "Luria's
  distinctive combination of schema flexibility and governance"; U12 and
  U13 are Study 1; U17 is Study 3. A36's "The key is to turn the
  distinctions developed in Nucleation into independently manipulated
  variables" is the owner's U15 request; A39's revision against prior
  research is U16's. A41 calls [QUESTION-388](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-388.md)'s note of 2026-11-07 a
  progression the record laid out; that note records A's own ladder from
  the exchange of 2026-11-06 to 07. A25 and A32 attribute their own coinages
  correctly ("representational plasticity", "shared epistemic state").
  Each entry filed credits the owner's turns.
- **(b) Coverage.** A45 drops the owner's U7 article framing and A20's
  maintenance benchmark; A17's prospective test record; A22's prior art
  beyond DILIGENT and EvoOntology; A25's migration criterion; A31's risks
  of bottleneck, amplification and lock-in; A32's false-consensus test and
  version distinction; A34's obstruction tasks and governance profile; and
  [QUESTION-072](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-072.md), which neither A45 nor A48 mentions. A48 restores [CLAIM-410](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-410.md)
  and [CASE-194](../../record/cases.d/CASE-194.md). Held entries the syntheses rebuild without citing:
  [CLAIM-266](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-266.md), [CASE-144](../../record/cases.d/CASE-144.md), [QUESTION-271](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-271.md), [CLAIM-299](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-299.md) and [SYNTHESIS-017](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-017.md). The
  filed entries restore each.
- **(c) Fidelity.** A cited about sixty codes, and its statuses, warrants
  and figures checked correct, as did luria's principles and [LU-ADR-035](https://github.com/dmarx/luria/blob/main/record/decisions.d/ADR-035.md). A48
  is right that [CASE-194](../../record/cases.d/CASE-194.md) is not [CLAIM-346](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-346.md)'s triple, which [CASE-194](../../record/cases.d/CASE-194.md) version 2
  also says. No misstatement of an entry's content was found beyond the
  attribution in (a).
- **(d) Standing.** A45 §1 calls six definitions, interpretive claims and
  an unrun study "a causal decomposition"; it is a decomposition by
  definition. A45 cites [CASE-186](../../record/cases.d/CASE-186.md) for "Correcting one failure does not imply
  retaining the capacity to correct a later failure", the premise of an
  unrun study, not a result. A36 cites [CLAIM-184](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-184.md) without marking it
  Proposed. The hedges are kept: A43's chart is hypothetical, A45 §8 says
  the proposed experiments have produced no results, A22 marks [ADR-084](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-084.md) and
  [ADR-082](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-082.md) Proposed.
- **(e) Integration.** One connecting claim across the eight accounts,
  [CLAIM-667](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-667.md); the rest recap held entries or are research questions.

## What was left, and why

- **The anthology's work** (U1 to U4, A1 to A12): left, belongs to the
  anthology, including A12's acquisition list (τ-bench, OSWorld and OSWorld
  2.0, SWE-bench Verified, Brynjolfsson, Li and Raymond, METR's 2025 study,
  AgentDojo, GraphCast), which A proposed as anthology sources.
- **A14's survey framing** of AI-assisted theory generation, its ladder of
  four capabilities and three feedback loops: A's summaries of works the
  record has not read, belonging in their readings; the works are
  registered.
- **Publication advice:** A20's venues (JASIST, Data & Knowledge
  Engineering, JCDL, JOSS, CSCW), working titles, and the term
  "governed representational plasticity" (A25), a label with nothing
  beyond [CLAIM-419](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-419.md) and [SYNTHESIS-012](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-012.md).
- **Planning detail** in the designs: pilot sizes, harness operations
  (A29, "not claims that Luria already provides each named function"),
  action-trace fields, power analysis, the YAML task specifications. The
  cases hold the designs, not the plans.
- **Further evaluations named but not designed here:** STATE-Bench and a
  longitudinal AstaBench (A27, A29), CooperBench and AsynCodeBench as
  transfer checks (A31, A39 Study F), MAPE-K with and without a governed
  substrate (A50), A34's full-record against compact standing-aware
  summaries, A50's novelty types and controlled code rigidity (in the note
  on [CLAIM-184](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-184.md)), A31's coordination penalty and recovery test, and A20's
  "curation completeness" task.
- **Proposals about this record's procedures**, offered to the owner, not
  filed as ADRs: A17's three additions to step 12 (rivals, discriminant,
  prospective result), its "epistemic critic" and "hypothesis packet",
  and its point that `defeated_if` is not a prediction recorded before the
  evidence; A20's retrospective audit of the [ADR-032](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-032.md), [ADR-061](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-061.md), [ADR-068](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-068.md),
  [ADR-075](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-075.md) and [ADR-084](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-084.md) episodes; A25's audit of misfits never recognized
  (the note on [CLAIM-419](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-419.md)).
- **The luria repository's business:** a luria memory adapter, A29's
  account of `luria migrate`, and anything about how luria should record
  which converses it wrote. Not checked here.
- **Works not registered:** Nii's blackboard papers (the DOI resolves, the
  title could not be confirmed); Oelen et al. 2019 (no verifiable
  identifier found); DILIGENT's 2004 ECAI paper (no identifier; the
  tradition is held as [LIT-2274](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2274.md)); "Stojanovic", "the Argument Web",
  Hamblin, and McBurney and Parsons (named without a work); PASC, ESEM 2026
  (its DOI does not resolve); the 2021 incident-response study of graceful
  extensibility, the 2025 review of self-driving laboratories, the
  design-science references and the conceptual-engineering literature
  (unnamed). Chen et al.'s survey of metamorphic testing (DOI
  10.1145/3143561) and Kiczales et al.'s *The Art of the Metaobject
  Protocol* (DOI 10.7551/mitpress/1405.001.0001) are verified but not
  registered: no word in the closed topic vocabulary holds software
  testing or reflective programming, and a word is added by decision.
- **The 13 title overlaps** A found between the records: the anthology's
  question, not checked here.

## Ideas offered

The filer offered five ideas of its own in its report; the owner accepted
all of them ("file their ideas too, I like ideas"). Each is in the
assistant's voice and Proposed.

1. **A curation-completeness study** built from the record's corrected
   filings: a proposed study, [CASE-251](../../record/cases.d/CASE-251.md), bearing on [QUESTION-108](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-108.md), with
   a pointer added to the note of 2026-11-12 on [QUESTION-108](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-108.md).
2. **The selection-bias count** for [CLAIM-419](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-419.md): cheap, so run. Filings of
   2026-11-07 and 2026-11-10 left 10 and 3 items, none for a grammar reason,
   and made no grammar amendment; this filing left one item (two works)
   for want of a topic word. Filed as a dated note on [CLAIM-419](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-419.md) with the
   method and its limit: the counts are a floor, and the source audit A25
   proposed is still the test.
3. **A THEORY for Halpern and Moses** from [NOTE-1381](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1381.md), which had none:
   [THEORY-1732](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1732.md), limited to the theorems [NOTE-1381](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1381.md) checked. [ARG-097](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-097.md)
   and [CLAIM-668](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-668.md) now ground on it instead of the bare [LIT-1213](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1213.md), and
   cite Theorem 8 (uncertain timing) in place of Theorems 7 and 11, whose
   proofs the note did not check.
4. **Recording which converses the tool wrote**, so a migration can tell
   forced relations from asserted ones: a design proposal for the luria
   tool, filed as a dated note on [CLAIM-666](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-666.md). The luria repository was
   not touched or consulted.
5. **A topic word for software engineering**, so that Chen et al.'s survey
   of metamorphic testing and Kiczales et al.'s *The Art of the Metaobject
   Protocol* can be registered: a decision about the vocabulary, filed as a
   Proposed ADR on its own branch, `claude/topic-software-engineering`,
   with those two works as its first application.

## Readings of 2026-11-12

The 92 works this filing touched were read the same day: the 59 the entry
of 2026-11-10 registered ([LIT-2271](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2271.md) to [LIT-2330](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2330.md)) and the 33 registered
above. Delegated readers drafted each reading in eight batches; the filer
checked each draft's metadata against Crossref, the arXiv API or the
work's own pages (no email address was sent to any service), filed a NOTE
and a THEORY for each work read, rechecked every quotation of six words or
more mechanically against the downloaded copy, the exchange or the entry
quoted, and kept as paraphrase, without quotation marks, any that did not
match. Copies were taken only from the lawful sources [ADR-074](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-074.md) counts. A
host that answered with a bot check, a challenge, a refusal or a paywall
was not retried, and a refusal by the session's permission system was not
worked around.

### Corrections to the exchange and to this filing

What A said of a work, checked against the work:

- **AstaBench** ([LIT-2299](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2299.md)) has no condition "with and without persistent
  structured records"; that was A's proposed study, and the benchmark as
  published gives an agent no carry-over between tasks.
- **OAEI** ([LIT-2302](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2302.md)) evaluates matching between ontologies, not
  "change-related interoperability"; it is not in [QUESTION-458](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-458.md)'s
  comparison class.
- **Kephart and Chess** ([LIT-2312](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2312.md)) never say "MAPE-K"; their loop is
  monitor, analyze, plan and execute over shared knowledge, and the name is
  later. [QUESTION-458](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-458.md)'s wording is corrected.
- **COPE** ([LIT-2479](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2479.md)) never names Edapt and does not introduce coupled
  evolution; it introduces COPE. That COPE became Edapt is known from
  outside the paper.
- **Salemi et al.'s blackboard system** ([LIT-2470](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2470.md)) carries requests for
  information between agents, not shared structured hypotheses or results.
- **BB1** ([LIT-2476](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2476.md), through [LIT-2472](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2472.md)): the 1985 paper's subject is
  a control blackboard holding the system's plan for its own problem
  solving; A's "shared structured hypotheses" fits the domain blackboard.
- **STAMP**: Patriarca et al. ([LIT-2477](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2477.md)) is a scoping, largely
  bibliometric review, not a statement of STAMP's causal thesis; [LIT-1613](../../record/literature.d/LIT-1613.md)
  is nearer to that.
- **Shumailov et al.** ([LIT-2480](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2480.md)): the record analogues in its
  registration summary are A's (A43), not the paper's.
- **PROV-O** ([LIT-2489](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2489.md)) represents origin, derivation, attribution and
  activity, and has no terms for support or standing, so it does not itself
  separate origin from support or standing, as A20 implied.
- **[LIT-2329](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2329.md)**: "revising a theory more readily is not necessarily better
  scientific behavior" is A's gloss (A14), not the paper's words; [CASE-188](../../record/cases.d/CASE-188.md)'s
  note is corrected.
- **Woods** ([LIT-2287](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2287.md)): the three-way split noted on [CASE-186](../../record/cases.d/CASE-186.md) is A's; Woods
  gives four senses of resilience, per Moerman et al. [CASE-186](../../record/cases.d/CASE-186.md)'s note is
  corrected.
- **Chang** ([LIT-2488](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2488.md)): the lecture notes read do not support A's
  reading that epistemic iteration revises what counts as a good update.
- **Stasser and Titus** ([LIT-2496](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2496.md)) never use the term "hidden profile",
  which came later.
- **ORKG** ([LIT-2510](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2510.md)): Allard Oelen is its second author; A's "Oelen et
  al. 2019" remains unidentified.
- **STATE-Bench** ([LIT-2296](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2296.md)): not reached; what A said of its tracks is
  unverified.

## Owner's review of 2026-11-12

The owner reviewed [#484](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/484) in chat on 2026-11-12 and asked for two changes.
Both were made on the same branch; every entry stays Proposed, and each
changed entry has a new version whose history cites the review.

**1. The central prediction narrowed.** "I'd separate the two into
independently testable predictions, or at least make the routine-task
prediction a secondary expectation rather than a defining part of the
principal claim." [CLAIM-667](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-667.md), version 2, now holds only the
interaction: governance raises the value of a modifiable schema on tasks
whose inherited categories are inadequate. Its title and defeat condition
no longer mention routine tasks; a benefit of governance that does not
depend on modifiability cancels in the interaction and does not defeat
it. The routine-task prediction is [CLAIM-665](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-665.md), a secondary thesis
with an empirical warrant, defeated by governance improving correction,
source verification, provenance or review quality on routine tasks by more
than it costs, a result that leaves [CLAIM-667](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-667.md) untouched. Neither
rests on the other: the owner's point is that the second does not follow
from the first. [CASE-253](../../record/cases.d/CASE-253.md) (version 2) names a secondary estimand for
it, reported apart; [ARG-098](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-098.md) (version 2, still Rejected) and
[SYNTHESIS-090](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-090.md) (version 2, which adds the new claim as a component)
follow the split.

**2. HiddenBench's Secretary brought into the main design.** "I'd update
the main design to include it, and specify whether the shared-notes
condition is intended to reproduce Secretary or provide something
different." [CASE-252](../../record/cases.d/CASE-252.md), version 2, adds two arms to its main table: AS,
the benchmark's Secretary, a passive shared summary of what has been
disclosed, and AS+, that summary written into the record's schemes by the
same non-participant. The shared-notes arm, A2, is stated not to
reproduce Secretary: agents write it, choosing what to post, its entries
persist and carry sources, and it can admit a clue never said aloud. A4
against AS is now an essential comparison beside A4 against A1. The case
says what would show the record wins only by doing Secretary's job better:
A3 or A4 beating AS while AS+ matches them and unique-clue coverage is no
higher than under AS. The change was not applied to [CASE-253](../../record/cases.d/CASE-253.md), whose
arms vary schema and governance and share no disclosed evidence, so a
Secretary arm has nothing to summarize there; nor to the other proposed
studies of this filing, none of which compares ways of sharing evidence.

On 2026-11-12 the owner asked for a batch of shared exchanges to be read
and filed. This entry files one of them: "Medical Ethics and Media
Enshitification" (https://chatgpt.com/share/6af5175d-c334-83ea-a02f-ef5752bd90d0,
2026-11-11 16:57 to 21:46 UTC, 21 owner turns U1–U21 and 44 assistant
turns A1–A44, of which 21 are substantive). It was decoded verbatim from
the share page and read in full from that file.

The exchange runs from medical ethics (abortion, circumcision, consent)
through the record (U4), microchimerism (U5–U6), the gut (U7–U8),
parasites (U9–U10), recommenders and dark patterns (U11), mobile games
(U12), the drift of content industries toward heavy users (U13–U15),
news (U16–U17) and normativity (U18–U21).

## Scope and method

The scope was set by the lead filer of the batch: a full map against the
record; an idea ledger; the owner's ideas filed as the owner's, and A's
filed where they have content of their own and are not held; ARGs where a
support is load-bearing or contested; dated notes; the synthesis audit;
and every cited work with a verifiable identifier registered unread unless
the owner supplied it. The owner's sources are to be read.

Following the `read-and-file` skill ([ADR-068](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-068.md)):

- The filer read every turn and kept a ledger, turn by turn, of the
  ideas, constructions, tables and works in it.
- Every record code A cited (over seventy) was looked up. A's statements
  of their status and content were right in every case checked, among
  them [CLAIM-354](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-354.md), [CLAIM-523](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-523.md) and [CLAIM-404](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-404.md) as Active, [TERM-083](../../record/terms.d/TERM-083.md), [THEORY-448](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-448.md),
  [CLAIM-555](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-555.md) and [CLAIM-624](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-624.md) as Proposed, [SYNTHESIS-007](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-007.md) superseded by
  [CLAIM-545](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-545.md), [CASE-123](../../record/cases.d/CASE-123.md)'s press variant, [QUESTION-364](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-364.md)'s three achievements
  and [NOTE-1096](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1096.md)'s habit/deliberation split.
- Every work A linked was checked against Crossref, DataCite, the arXiv
  API, Europe PMC or its own page, and searched in the record by DOI,
  arXiv id, URL and title. One was held: Pettigrew's "Consent and the
  Formation of Preferences" ([LIT-202](../../record/literature.d/LIT-202.md)).
- Every quotation of six words or more in the new entries and notes was
  checked mechanically against the decoded exchange, the sources read,
  or the record entry quoted. Every computation in A's text that a filed
  entry leans on was recomputed: 150/245 = 61.2%, d* = 2/2.95 = 0.678,
  the $30.50 net, the geometric acquisition costs ($70 median, $100 mean,
  $228 at the 90th percentile, $83.8 with a guarantee at draw 90), the
  composition identity and the inclusions K_uniform ⊆ K_each ⊆ K_some.
  All hold.

No. No entry cites the share link. The record held nothing on
circumcision, Toxoplasma, Cordyceps, whaling, clickbait, the attention
economy, PASS@(k,T) or pass@k. Its only mention of microchimerism was in
passing in [NOTE-100](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-100.md). What it did hold are the neighbours mapped below.

**Findings, by check.**

- *Attribution.* A mostly credited the owner ("you're identifying a
  potentially important cross-scale preference-amplification mechanism",
  A27; "This is very close to your original proposal", A29). The risk is
  in naming. A restated the owner's U13 mechanism as its own proposal ("The
  general mechanism I'd propose is", A29) and gave it A's names
  ("revenue-weighted preference selection", "revenue-weighted selection of
  consumer environments"), and the recaps (A33, A35) carry those names
  without the owner. The filed entries credit the mechanism, the loot-box
  test and the PASS@(k,T) link to the owner, and A's names and derivations
  to A.
- *Coverage.* The recaps (A33, A35, A39) drop the owner's escalation half
  of U13 and the microchimerism and parasite lines, keeping only the
  economic and normative strands. A37's line map is complete for the
  line.
- *Fidelity.* No record entry was misstated. A35 says the Montero-Porras
  model is "not independent proof of Doctorow's historical claims", which
  is right. A42 says its K_uniform/K_each/K_some is "not a complete
  novelty at the mathematical level", which is right: it is [CLAIM-537](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-537.md)'s
  ∀∃ against ∃∀.
- *Standing.* A mostly marked its own Proposed and unverified items. One
  slip: A44 states PASS@(k,T)'s monotonicity in T as a property, which the
  paper asserts and its own per-depth estimates do not show
  ([NOTE-1749](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1749.md)).
- *Integration.* The theses add labels ("trajectory-level capture",
  "endogenous erosion of corrective capacity", "normatively
  self-insulating", "normative capability frontier") to combinations the
  record holds. Where one passed admission, a derivation ([CLAIM-662](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-662.md))
  or a sharper separation ([CLAIM-661](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-661.md)), it was filed.

No SYNTHESIS was revised. The new entries on the organizational-normativity

## What was left, and why

- **The bioethics survey (A2–A5).** A's map of others' positions: five
  theories of moral status, Thomson's violinist and its objections, three
  models of autonomy, the three levels of moral, professional and legal
  analysis, the right to an open future, and A5's eight connections (IVF
  embryos and LePage, embryo models and organoids, advance requests for
  assisted dying, OTOF gene therapy, embryo selection and the
  non-identity problem, surrogacy, normothermic regional perfusion, and
  reproductive surveillance with clinical AI). These are reports of a
  literature, not ideas of A's own. Their linked works are registered;
  the one question with content of its own, surrogate authority, is
  [QUESTION-454](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-454.md). A3's three rights and A9's three dimensions
  (welfare, bodily integrity, legitimate authority) are quoted there and
  not filed separately.
- **Passing points.** These have no content beyond their sentence: A11 §6
  on whether a mother keeps authority over her cells in her child (A
  answers no), and consent for tissue samples that carry a relative's
  cells. Also A13's ethics-first metaphysics, a pointer to Żuradzki
  ([LIT-2382](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2382.md)); A21's AI-companionship trial and Wolbachia dengue
  trial; and A25's four regulatory objectives and its two $500 players,
  which are [CASE-128](../../record/cases.d/CASE-128.md) and [CASE-109](../../record/cases.d/CASE-109.md)'s contrast. A35's AI answer engines
  ("downstream access" against "upstream discovery capacity"), scientific
  publishing, the creator economy and information voids are further
  instances of [CLAIM-656](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-656.md)'s capability displacement and [CLAIM-404](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-404.md),
  noted where they bear. A42's Doughnut thresholds and future bearers of
  demands are a domain for [QUESTION-456](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-456.md), and its actual, demonstrated
  and unresolved compatibility is [QUESTION-279](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-279.md)'s distinction.
- **Owner's requests with no idea of their own** (U1–U4, U6, U10, U15,
  U17, U20) are recorded as the prompts of what they produced.
- **Works without a verifiable identifier**, left unregistered: those A
  cited only through its search tool (the `Cite` references), among them
  the Anesthesia & Analgesia piece on conscientious objection, Kogan 2023,
  Buckler's "The Smallest Cut", the ESHRE and ISSCR statements, the
  Häyry–Sukenick and Marquis papers, Canada's Bill C-41, the studies
  behind A19's parasite cases, the Mendelian-randomization null, the
  NEJM Wolbachia trial, the 263- and 380-participant experiments, Pew's
  Twitter and AI-summary analyses, the Reuters Institute and Medill
  reports, Zendle and colleagues' 69-million-player study, DoubleVerify's
  AutoBait report, Shumailov and colleagues' model-collapse paper, the
  fabricated-references study and the FTC's Genshin Impact settlement.
  Two linked works could not be verified: the INN Index report (HTTP 403)
  and the Tampere repository PDF on recommender fairness (a bot check).
  A later pass can identify the unlinked works by search.

## Ideas offered

The filer offered five ideas of its own after the filing (skill step 12).
The owner accepted all of them on 2026-11-12 ("file their ideas too, I
like ideas"). Each is the assistant's and Proposed:

1. **Exit-driven drift as a route to occlusion.** Filed as [CLAIM-652](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-652.md),
   demonstrated as a possibility, bearing on [QUESTION-441](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-441.md). It is grounded
   in a toy built and run with python3 -I ([CASE-246](../../record/cases.d/CASE-246.md)) and argued in
   [ARG-092](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-092.md). The model corrected the idea as offered. Recognized
   complaints do not fall; they rise more slowly than the harm, while the
   practice rises from 0.05 to 0.223 with no act against complaint.
2. **The scope of [CLAIM-560](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-560.md)'s monotonicity.** Filed as [CLAIM-654](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-654.md),
   demonstrated, with the proof in its body, construction [CASE-245](../../record/cases.d/CASE-245.md)
   and [ARG-086](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-086.md). The three-state construction and an exhaustive check
   of the 27 stationary successor maps were verified. PASS@(k,T)'s
   Figure 1 is cited only as a possible witness, with its 64-rollout
   caveat.
3. **Activity weighting as a [CLAIM-348](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-348.md) coarse-graining.** It restates
   [CLAIM-348](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-348.md) for one coarse-graining, so it is a dated note on [CLAIM-348](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-348.md)
   with a checked witness: two populations with the same sessions and the
   same activity-weighted share, and opposite majorities.
4. **The Peng depletion result and [CLAIM-530](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-530.md)'s parthood clause.** A
   proposed test, filed as a dated note on [QUESTION-086](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-086.md) with a pointer on
   [CLAIM-530](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-530.md). The Immunity paper ([LIT-2462](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2462.md)) is Unfetched, and the
   reading is owed.
5. **Provenance of an authorization ([TERM-100](../../record/terms.d/TERM-100.md)) for surrogate authority.**
   An interpretive mapping, filed as a dated note on [QUESTION-454](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-454.md).

None is a decision about the record's rules, so no ADR was filed.

## Owner's review of 2026-11-12

The owner reviewed [#485](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/485) in chat on 2026-11-12 and asked for three changes.
Each changed entry carries a new version whose history cites the review.
Everything stays Proposed.

1. **[CLAIM-662](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-662.md) narrowed (version 2).** The owner pointed out that the
   derivation's step 2 did not follow: a count of satisfied demands rises
   when a met demand is newly recognized. The claim now states the owner's
   form: "For a fixed arrangement, expanding the recognized demand set
   cannot improve conjunctive compliance and cannot decrease the count of
   recognized violations. Where governance penalizes newly recognized
   violations without rewarding their discovery, the organization may
   acquire an incentive to avoid improving its normative identification."
   The two monotonicity facts are demonstrated; the incentive is
   conditional on the governance assumption.
   - The owner's table of four scores was checked with python3 -I over
     every satisfaction pattern and every D_0 ⊊ D_1, for 2 demands (20
     cases) and 3 demands (152 cases). Pass never rose, violations never
     fell, the count satisfied never fell and rose in 11 and 91 cases, and
     the fraction rose in 2 and 30 cases and fell in 2 and 30.
   - Entries that repeated the old wording were corrected: [CLAIM-347](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md)
     (version 4), [CLAIM-475](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-475.md) (version 5), [QUESTION-441](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-441.md) (version 4) and
     [CLAIM-652](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-652.md)'s defeated_if (version 2).
   - [ARG-093](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-093.md) neither concludes nor uses [CLAIM-662](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-662.md), so it is
     unchanged. [CASE-249](../../record/cases.d/CASE-249.md) uses only step 1, which stands, so it is
     unchanged too.
2. **[CASE-245](../../record/cases.d/CASE-245.md) corrected (version 2).** Under its architecture (s to g,
   s to t, t absorbing) a stochastic stationary process taking s to g with
   probability p succeeds with probability p at every b ≥ 1, not
   1 − (1 − p)^b. A variant with an explicit self-loop gives 1 − (1 − p)^b,
   and with a trap as well, p(1 − r^b)/(1 − r). All three were computed
   exactly, as fractions, for p = 1/3 and 1/2 and b = 0 to 5. [CLAIM-654](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-654.md)
   and [ARG-086](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-086.md) do not repeat the formula and are unchanged. The main
   counterexample stands.
3. **The owner's refinement of [QUESTION-441](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-441.md).** It separates two routes by
   which an organization becomes less informed without censoring anyone:
   selective disappearance ([CLAIM-652](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-652.md)) and costly discovery
   ([CLAIM-662](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-662.md)). Neither is deliberate suppression, and both are
   distinct from the counter-corrective model ([CLAIM-619](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-619.md)). The record did
   not hold the distinction: [CLAIM-624](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-624.md) separates occlusion,
   self-certification and reproduction, not these routes. It is filed as
   the owner's [CLAIM-657](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-657.md), interpretive, resting on both claims, with a
   defeated_if for a single mechanism behind both routes or routes that
   cannot be told apart. A dated note on [QUESTION-441](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-441.md) points to it.

On 2026-11-12 the owner asked for the exchange "About Plantation
Paradise" (https://chatgpt.com/share/6af620a9-b0f8-83e8-8d25-b42434630c81,
2026-11-12 18:19 to 19:44 UTC; five owner turns, U1 to U5, and twelve
replies, A1 to A12) to be read and filed. The filing followed the
`read-and-file` skill ([ADR-068](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-068.md)), from the verbatim decoded export.

**Scope, set by the lead.** The full map against the record; an idea
ledger; the owner's ideas filed, and A's where they have content of
their own and are not held; ARGs where support is load-bearing or
contested; dated notes on the entries the exchange bears on; the
synthesis audit; this entry and a changelog fragment; and the
acknowledgements. The works A cited were checked for held-ness and
identifiers and registered unread as Deferred LITs, left for a reading
pass. The owner supplied no link to a work, so nothing was read in this
filing. One filer did the whole pass; no readers were delegated. Every
quotation of the exchange in the new entries and notes was checked
mechanically against the export.

## The exchange, turn by turn

- **U1, U2** (the owner): U1 asked about "plantation to paradise", and
  U2 to "tell me more about the theory discussed by the book and
  subsequent works in conversation with it". A1 identified the book as
  David M. Powers's *From Plantation to Paradise?* (2014), and the owner
  confirmed at U2.
- **A3**: Powers's arguments (culture as colonial governance; the
  theatre's racially divided seating, its *paradis*; Black performers'
  participation as both domination and agency), Mondelli's review,
  Prest's work and the Leichman and Bénac-Giroux volume, a table of
  theorists, three open problems and a reading sequence.
- **U3** (the owner): "connect to the [nucleation] record's
  investigations of dependency formation, exploitation identification,
  and the contextual/conditional nature of organizational normativity".
- **A6**: the colonial theatre read against the record, in five problems
  and a synthesis.
- **U4** (the owner): whether the discussion is in conversation with
  contemporary research "which isn't currently reflected on the
  Nucleation record".
- **A9**: racialized organizations, predatory inclusion, complaint,
  inhabited institutionalism, Black feminist archival history and
  gaslighting, with a gap audit against the record.
- **U5** (the owner): "is there anything in this neighborhood that
  investigates the question from  the abstract perspective of probing
  the nature of obligations a whole might have towards its constituent
  parts?"
- **A12**: what a whole owes its parts: Goodin, Kittay, group agency,
  Fineman, environmental holism and Thompson, with a proposed
  formulation and a candidate principle.
- **A2, A4, A5, A7, A8, A10, A11** are progress notes between tool calls.
  A5 and A8 anticipate A6 and A9 and add nothing they do not.

## Where the record already held it

The exchange was not on the record: no entry cites its share id, and
none holds Powers or the colonial theatre. The record's uses of
"plantation" ([NOTE-115](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-115.md), [NOTE-706](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-706.md), [NOTE-951](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-951.md), [NOTE-1089](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1089.md), [NOTE-1365](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1365.md),
[NOTE-1659](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1659.md), [NOTE-1660](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1660.md), [NOTE-1665](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1665.md), [NOTE-1674](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1674.md), [SYNTHESIS-010](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-010.md), and [CASE-169](../../record/cases.d/CASE-169.md)'s
Chagos plantation society) are forest plantations, the Kirtland's
Warbler's planted habitat, the Black Belt's plantation counties, the
Chagos copra plantations, and the words "implantation" and
"transplantation". None bears on the book.

Most of A's analysis applies entries the record holds, and A cited them
accurately. The checks are in the dated notes of 2026-11-12.

- **A6 §1, dependency formation.** Formation, persistence and
  maintenance kept apart is [CLAIM-566](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-566.md). The open transition to a
  self-maintaining nucleus is [QUESTION-399](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-399.md), and independence from what
  founds a structure but not from what feeds it is [CLAIM-597](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-597.md). Both are
  cited accurately. Capability lost to a reliable supplier is [CLAIM-603](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-603.md),
  in the transient-support line with [CLAIM-600](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md), [CLAIM-602](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md), [CLAIM-605](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-605.md) and
  [SYNTHESIS-032](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-032.md). Partners coming to depend on one another is
  [QUESTION-277](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-277.md) and [SYNTHESIS-053](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-053.md).
- **A6 §2, exploitation identification.** Stable coexistence is not
  cooperation: [CLAIM-546](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-546.md). The same dependence organized as opportunity,
  vulnerability or coercive leverage: [CLAIM-428](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-428.md). A's "transition from
  dependency to domination" is [CLAIM-428](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-428.md)'s third mode, with the holder
  of influence named (note on [CLAIM-428](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-428.md)). Freedom as governance of one's
  own governability is [CLAIM-545](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-545.md). A's objection "Reciprocity is not
  enough" is [CLAIM-428](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-428.md) applied to [CLAIM-603](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-603.md)'s reciprocal form, and
  [CLAIM-603](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-603.md) already concedes it (note on [CLAIM-603](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-603.md)). A's five predicates
  (contribution, dependency, cooperation, exploitation, domination) are
  kept in the note on [CLAIM-546](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-546.md). The record's other exploitation entries
  are Berenstain's *Epistemic Exploitation* ([LIT-2264](../../record/literature.d/LIT-2264.md), Deferred) and, for
  access without authority, [CLAIM-403](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-403.md).
- **A6 §3, legibility.** [CLAIM-348](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-348.md) and [CASE-110](../../record/cases.d/CASE-110.md) are cited accurately,
  numbers included. The archival extension, with A9 §6's "Inadequate

  to the historian's evidence, and [CLAIM-657](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-657.md) is the organization's own

- **A6 §4, conditional normativity.** [CLAIM-363](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-363.md), [CLAIM-075](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-075.md), [QUESTION-129](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-129.md)

  the scope of [SYNTHESIS-038](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-038.md).

## What was filed

**The owner's.**

  whole has towards its own constituent parts, and on what ground. It is
  on the organizational-normativity line and refines [QUESTION-128](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-128.md). The
  record held the direction only as the set-aside authenticity line's

## Syntheses audited

Three distinct theses. Each is A's.

1. **A6's central proposal, with §7 "A possible theoretical synthesis"
   and its closing thesis.** Proposed. A6: "An organization can become
   dependent upon the contributions of a subordinated population while
   remaining organized to prevent that population's causal importance
   from acquiring corresponding normative authority." It separates
   productive-dependency, authority and normative-legibility structures,
   which "Nothing guarantees ... coincide", and adds a stronger
   reproductive hypothesis. A9 §9's candidate thesis is a second version
   of the same thesis.
   - *Decomposition.* That the three structures can diverge is
     [CLAIM-428](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-428.md) (a dependence does not fix who holds influence),
     [CLAIM-403](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-403.md) (admission apart from a part in revising the standards)
     and [CLAIM-462](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-462.md) (effective action and correctability kept by
     different relations). The closing thesis, "we cannot adequately
     judge an organization by examining only the relations that sustain
     it", is [CLAIM-075](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-075.md) with [CLAIM-348](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-348.md). The reproductive hypothesis is
     [CLAIM-614](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-614.md) for parties the organization depends on.
   - *Attribution.* The owner's U3 framing, three investigations, is
     told as "the nucleation record's" five problems. That is fair: A6
     asked for nothing more. A6 marks its own formulations as its own.
   - *Coverage.* It drops [CLAIM-403](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-403.md) and [CLAIM-462](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-462.md), the record's closest
     entries, and the transient-support account ([SYNTHESIS-032](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-032.md)).
   - *Fidelity.* It says the objection to [CLAIM-603](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-603.md) "exposes a
     limitation"; [CLAIM-603](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-603.md) already concedes it.
   - *Standing.* Each cited entry's status is given correctly.
   - *Integration.* The divergence of the three structures is held, and
     the closing thesis is a recap. The reproductive hypothesis is
     existential ("some institutions") and passes no route as a claim.
     What it leaves open, when dependence becomes authority, is filed as
     [QUESTION-461](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-461.md). No claim filed.
2. **A9 §9 to §10, "three increasingly ambitious levels" and "The
   broader discovery".** Proposed, about the record's prospects. It adds
   one claim about novelty: parts of A6's synthesis "should be understood
   as converging with established racialized-organizations theory rather
   than as entirely new theoretical discoveries".
   That is unverified until Ray is read, and it is noted in Ray's LIT. No
   claim filed.
3. **A12 §7 to §10 and its close.** Proposed. Grounds of a whole's
   obligations, "a candidate research question", and a candidate
   principle.
   - *Coverage.* A12 misses the record's nearest entries, among them
     the owner's own earlier statement of the direction: [CLAIM-104](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-104.md) (U75
     of an earlier exchange, Deferred), [QUESTION-007](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-007.md), [SYNTHESIS-023](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-023.md)'s
     finding that the downward norm's content is unstated, [CLAIM-362](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-362.md)'s
     "not asserting rights for neural modules", [TERM-083](../../record/terms.d/TERM-083.md) (moral
     standing), [CLAIM-511](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-511.md) and [QUESTION-454](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-454.md).
   - *Attribution.* "Your question is principally about C" credits U5
     correctly.
   - *Fidelity.* Its uses of [CLAIM-075](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-075.md), [QUESTION-128](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-128.md), [CLAIM-518](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-518.md),
     [CLAIM-545](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-545.md) and [CLAIM-624](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-624.md) are faithful.
   - *Integration.* The candidate research question goes into
     [QUESTION-460](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-460.md) as A's sharpening. The candidate principle passes
     as a discriminating prediction, conditional on Goodin's principle,
     and is filed as [CLAIM-671](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-671.md), role supposed; its "Admission"
     section gives the route. The closing expectation, a relational
     account in which "organizational facts determine who owes what to
     whom" and "further normative principles determine why", restates
     [QUESTION-128](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-128.md)'s two halves and is noted there.

A3 §6's summary of the scholarship (Powers, then Prest and others) is
about the literature, not the record. It is descriptive and unverified,
and its content is in [CASE-257](../../record/cases.d/CASE-257.md) and the LITs. None of the three
theses is an account of a line of the record. Each applies the
organizational-normativity line to an outside case or question. So no
SYNTHESIS was revised, and [SYNTHESIS-038](../../record/syntheses.d/SYNTHESIS-038.md) gets a note naming the new
entries for the line's synthesis review.

## Support judgements, and why no ARG was filed

Every place the filing says one entry supports, qualifies or fails to
support another:

- [CASE-257](../../record/cases.d/CASE-257.md) `illustrates` [CLAIM-546](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-546.md), [CLAIM-403](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-403.md) and [CLAIM-348](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-348.md). These
  are plain illustrations, with nothing said about strength.
- [CLAIM-671](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-671.md) `rests_on` [CLAIM-603](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-603.md). A claim's own `rests_on` needs no
  ARG.
- The note on [CLAIM-603](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-603.md) says A's objection bounds what "reciprocity" can
  be read to promise. It finds the claim already concedes the point, so
  no support relation is doubted.
- The note on [CLAIM-348](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-348.md) says A9 §6's point is [CLAIM-350](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-350.md) applied to the
  historian's evidence. That is a mapping of an unfiled idea, not support
  between entries.
- [CLAIM-669](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-669.md) and [CLAIM-671](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-671.md) cite unread works in their bodies
  and carry no `grounds`. Their support is A's report, and their status,
  Proposed, says so.

None is load-bearing or contested in [ADR-061](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-061.md)'s sense, so no ARG was
filed. The reading pass on the registered works is where `grounds`,
`corroborates` and their ARGs would arise.

## Readings of 2026-11-12

The owner asked for the registered works to be read ("read the works you
can reach"). Readers read the twenty-five works in three batches (pp-1,
pp-2, pp-3), with lawful copies only, and wrote drafts outside the
repository. The filer checked every quotation the filing leans on against
the downloaded text by script, corrected the LITs from the text, and filed
the readings. [ADR-068](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-068.md)'s invariants held: no email address went to any
service, and every bot check ended the attempt on that host.

### The owner's correction: which sense of "organization"

During the pass the owner wrote: "keep in mind, my use of 'organization'
is more abstract than standin for 'institution'. check the TERM." The term
is [TERM-074](../../record/terms.d/TERM-074.md), whose default sense 1 is a relational arrangement. So:

- [QUESTION-460](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-460.md) (version 2) now says that its "organized whole" is
  [TERM-074](../../record/terms.d/TERM-074.md) sense 1 by default. A whole in that sense need not be an
  institution or an agent: an organism and its cells, an ecosystem, an
  arrangement of processes. It also states the question's prior part
  inside its body: whether, and in which of A12's senses of obligation, a
  whole that is not an agent can bear obligations at all. [QUESTION-128](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-128.md)
  holds the functional sense; [CLAIM-104](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-104.md) and [TERM-083](../../record/terms.d/TERM-083.md) do not hold the rest,
  so the part stays in the question rather than becoming an entry of its
  own.
- [CLAIM-671](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-671.md) (version 2) and [ARG-099](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-099.md) declare their sense. The
  claim's integration is sense 1. Its consequent reaches only wholes that
  can bear responsibility, and only parts with standing.
- Every reading's bearing names the sense it is about. Lovett and
  Riedener, Thompson, Fineman, Goodin, Kittay, Ahmed, Fuentes and the
  colonial-theatre works are about sense 3, collective institutions and
  persons. They bear on the owner's question only for such wholes, and
  none answers it in sense 1. Wardrope's Land Ethic community is closer to
  sense 1, but there the obligation is borne by the members, as agents,
  and not by the whole.

### What the readings changed

- **[CASE-257](../../record/cases.d/CASE-257.md), version 2.** Minette and Lise were free women of
  colour. Enslaved people took part as musicians, supernumeraries,
  wigmakers, painters and builders. The seating is Prest's: second-tier
  boxes in Port-au-Prince and upper back boxes in Le Cap. The *paradis* is
  A's or Powers's and unverified. "Pale imitations" corrects A3 on three
  points: no staged chica is documented, vodou dance was not staged, and
  the framework is Roque's, not Bhabha's. The sentence on Créole
  performance is A3's inference; the editors' blog does not carry it.
- **[CLAIM-669](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-669.md), version 2.** It is narrowed after Seamster and
  Charron-Chénier. Their access arrangement leaves a lasting encumbrance
  but does not produce the need: the need predates the access, the
  encumbrance is debt, and exit is closed by bankruptcy law. [ARG-100](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-100.md)
  (Proposed) records the contested support.
- **[CLAIM-671](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-671.md), versions 2 and 3.** Version 2 declares the claim's
  sense; [ARG-099](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-099.md) (Rejected) finds that Fineman does not support it as
  titled. Version 3 adds to its defeat condition a route its defeaters did
  not list: transferring the parts' vulnerability to another protector,
  from Carroll and Crutchfield's restatement of Goodin. Goodin's own text
  was not read, and the claim stays Proposed. The supposition is
  confirmed as Goodin's, but the consequent is not shown to be his. The
  APSR abstract's "criteria of a morally acceptable dependency
  relationship" and Kittay's caution against domination by supporters
  qualify the claim (dated note).
- **Relations written** ([ADR-093](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-093.md)):
  - `corroborates`:
    - [CLAIM-075](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-075.md), from Lovett and Riedener, and from Thompson;

## Owner's review of 2026-11-13

The owner reviewed [#488](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/488) on 2026-11-13 (comment 6839732083) and asked for
five changes. The review reads as written with ChatGPT; the owner adopted
its requests by posting them, and they are attributed to "the owner's
review of [#488](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/488) on 2026-11-13". Everything stays Proposed. Each changed
entry has a new version whose history cites the review.

- **The ground and the bearer ([QUESTION-460](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-460.md), version 3).** The title
  now asks whether an organized whole grounds norms concerning its parts
  and who bears the obligations they establish: the whole, where it can
  owe, or the agents and roles that maintain, control or benefit from the
  arrangement. A section, "Ground and bearer: two inquiries", quotes the
  review: "A whole can be the ground or object of a normative judgment
  without necessarily being the bearer of the corresponding obligation."
  The record did not hold the distinction. [TERM-083](../../record/terms.d/TERM-083.md) separates moral agents
  from moral patients, which is about who is owed, and is cited as the
  nearest. [QUESTION-128](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-128.md) and [CLAIM-104](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-104.md) do not separate ground from bearer.
- **The discriminating test ([CASE-256](../../record/cases.d/CASE-256.md), new).** The review's matched
  pair holds vulnerability, the controllers' capacities and the
  consequences fixed, and varies only membership. It is stated in the
  question's body, with its three-result table, and filed as a stipulated
  thought experiment bearing on the question. The record files a
  construction that discriminates among answers as a CASE ([ADR-042](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-042.md)), and
  [ADR-072](../../record/decisions.d/ADR-072.md) codes an idea with content of its own.
- **[CLAIM-671](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-671.md), version 4.** Retitled to the review's proposition:
  "Where an organizational transformation increases a constituent's
  vulnerability to the discretionary choices of a responsible agent, and
  that vulnerability grounds special obligations under an independently
  justified principle, the transformation can strengthen that agent's
  responsibilities toward the constituent."
  - A section records the review's point that integration need not
    monotonically increase vulnerability: it can bring alternatives,
    shared governance, guarantees and a distribution of responsibility.
  - The bearer is now an agent, not the whole. `defeated_if` and the
    summary are rewritten to match.
  - It no longer rests on [CLAIM-603](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-603.md), which the body keeps as one route.
  - The role stays `supposed`: the claim still holds only if a principle
    the record does not hold is granted.
  - [ARG-099](../../record/arguments.d/ARG-099.md) (version 2) is retitled to the new claim and rechecked;
    it is still Rejected.
  - [NOTE-1899](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1899.md) (version 2), [NOTE-1900](../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1900.md) (version 2) and
    [THEORY-1818](../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1818.md) (version 2) restate their paraphrases of the claim.
    The claim's own dated notes of 2026-11-12 keep their wording, which
    was true when written.
- **[CLAIM-669](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-669.md), version 3, and [CLAIM-670](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-670.md), new.** The summary now
  follows version 2 and drops the unread-source characterization. The
  review asked to keep "the distinction between producing a dependency
  and producing a new encumbrance within an existing dependency".
  - The record held the first mechanism nowhere: [CLAIM-603](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-603.md) holds how
    supply produces a reliance, not its use to set terms.
  - So A's original sense is filed as [CLAIM-670](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-670.md), Proposed, resting
    on [CLAIM-603](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-603.md) and complementing [CLAIM-669](../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-669.md).
  - No reading supports it yet.
  - The changelog line that said "produces the dependence" is corrected.
- **[CASE-257](../../record/cases.d/CASE-257.md), version 3.** The title states the documented
  allocation: contribution, and exclusion from standing. The causal
  reading, that seating, casting and law kept the contributions from
  giving standing, moves into "Observation and interpretation" as an
  interpretation, with other mechanisms that fit the same allocation, for
  [QUESTION-461](../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-461.md) to test.
